[package]
name = "scrutate-py"
version = "0.1.0"
edition.workspace = true
rust-version.workspace = true
repository.workspace = true
description = "Python bindings for the Scrutate code-search engines (PyO3, stable ABI)"
license.workspace = true
publish = false

[lib]
name = "scrutate"
crate-type = ["cdylib"]

[dependencies]
# abi3-py39: one wheel per OS/architecture serves every CPython >= 3.9
pyo3 = { version = "0.30", features = ["abi3-py39", "abi3t"] }
scrutate = { path = "../scrutate" }
serde_json = "1"
anyhow = "1"

[features]
default = []
# forwarded to the engine: the optional heavy grammars
extra-langs = ["scrutate/extra-langs"]

# scrutate (Python bindings)

Python access to the Scrutate engines through PyO3, built with maturin against the stable ABI:
per operating system and architecture, one `abi3` wheel for standard CPython 3.9 to 3.14, one
`abi3t` wheel for 3.15 and newer (standard and free-threaded), and a `cp314t` wheel for
free-threaded 3.14.

```python
import scrutate

# Engine A: index-free search, streamed as the files are scanned
for m in scrutate.grep("refresh_token", ["."], mode="literal"):
    print(m.path, m.line, m.text)

# Engine B: the persistent code-intelligence index
repo = scrutate.Repo(".")
repo.index()                       # incremental; releases the GIL while it runs
for hit in repo.search("where do we refresh expired tokens", k=5):
    print(hit.path, hit.start, hit.qualname, hit.score)
```

The GIL is released during indexing and searching, so several Python threads can drive the
engines in parallel. `grep` returns an iterator fed by a background search thread; results are
converted to Python objects one batch at a time, never materialised as one giant list.

`grep` checks its arguments when it is called: `ValueError` for a bad pattern, glob or file type
or no paths, `FileNotFoundError` for a path that does not exist. Matches come in the order the
files are searched; `sort=True` gives path and line order (the first match then waits for the
whole search). `Repo.read` raises `FileNotFoundError` for a missing file and `ValueError` for a
path outside the repository. Ctrl-C stops a `grep` or a `Repo.index()` within about 100 ms; an
interrupted update stops at its next batch of files and leaves the index as it was.

`Repo.symbol`, `Repo.callers`, `Repo.duplicates` and the hits of `Repo.callees` come as a
`scrutate.Results` list. It is a `list` with one more field: `stopped_at` is the limit when more
results were left, else `None`.
`Repo.callers` also says how sure the resolver was: `undecided` counts the callers it kept
without knowing whether they call this definition or another of the same name.

Every `Repo` method runs the operation the CLI and the MCP tools run, with the same defaults,
the same check of the files an answer cites, and the same recovery from a damaged index.
`Repo.references(name, max_results=200, textual=False, definition=None)` gives the `references`
answer as a dict (`scrutate refs --json`'s `result`). `Repo.call(tool, args, max_bytes=None,
offset=0)` runs any MCP tool by its name and arguments, `grep_code` with a `mode`, a `path` and
`globs` included, and returns the tool's envelope as a dict: `schema`, `result`, `stopped_at`
when the answer stopped at its limit, and `text`, the text form from item `offset` on within
`max_bytes`. `GrepIter.stats()` lists in `notes` the (path, text) of each file whose search a
NUL byte stopped after a match: a match after that byte is not in the results.

[build-system]
requires = ["maturin>=1.14,<2"]
build-backend = "maturin"

[project]
name = "scrutate"
description = "Universal instant code search and persistent code intelligence (Rust engines, Python bindings)"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.9"
license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"
# the notices are written by tools/third_party_notices.py before a release build
license-files = ["LICENSE-APACHE", "LICENSE-MIT", "THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES*"]
dynamic = ["version"]
classifiers = [
  "Programming Language :: Rust",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: Implementation :: CPython",
  "Operating System :: OS Independent",
  "Topic :: Software Development",
]

[tool.maturin]
module-name = "scrutate._native"
python-source = "python"
strip = true

"""Scrutate: universal instant code search (Engine A) and persistent code intelligence (Engine B).

Everything here is implemented in Rust (`scrutate._native`); this package only re-exports it.
"""
from ._native import Match, Hit, Repo, GrepIter, Results, grep, version, __version__  # noqa: F401

__all__ = ["Match", "Hit", "Repo", "GrepIter", "Results", "grep", "version", "__version__"]

[package]
name = "scrutate"
version = "0.1.0"
edition.workspace = true
rust-version.workspace = true
repository.workspace = true
description = "Scrutate: universal instant code search (Engine A) and a persistent code-intelligence index with learned ranking (Engine B), one CLI and MCP server"
license.workspace = true

[[bin]]
name = "scrutate"
path = "src/main.rs"

[package.metadata.deb]
maintainer = "Cris Nahine <80492222+crisnahine@users.noreply.github.com>"
section = "devel"
extended-description = "Instant grep-class search of any repository without an index, plus a persistent index for ranked search, symbols, callers and imports. One CLI and an MCP server."
assets = [
    ["target/release/scrutate", "usr/bin/", "755"],
    ["../../LICENSE-APACHE", "usr/share/doc/scrutate/", "644"],
    ["../../LICENSE-MIT", "usr/share/doc/scrutate/", "644"],
    ["../../README.md", "usr/share/doc/scrutate/", "644"],
    # written by packaging/linux/build-packages.sh
    ["THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt", "usr/share/doc/scrutate/", "644"],
]

[package.metadata.generate-rpm]
summary = "Instant code search and a persistent code-intelligence index"
assets = [
    { source = "target/release/scrutate", dest = "/usr/bin/scrutate", mode = "755" },
    { source = "../../LICENSE-APACHE", dest = "/usr/share/licenses/scrutate/LICENSE-APACHE", mode = "644", doc = true },
    { source = "../../LICENSE-MIT", dest = "/usr/share/licenses/scrutate/LICENSE-MIT", mode = "644", doc = true },
    { source = "../../README.md", dest = "/usr/share/doc/scrutate/README.md", mode = "644", doc = true },
    { source = "THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt", dest = "/usr/share/licenses/scrutate/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt", mode = "644", doc = true },
]

aho-corasick = "1"
anyhow = "1"
blake2 = "0.10"

# The gate job of .github/workflows/benchmarks.yml in a clean container. The run steps are read
# from the workflow file itself, so this cannot drift from it; the commit to measure against is
# BASE (default: the parent of HEAD). Only what is committed is cloned.
#
#   docker run --rm -e BASE=<commit> -v "$PWD":/src:ro python:3.13-slim-bookworm bash /src/tools/bench_rehearsal.sh
set -euo pipefail
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive CARGO_TERM_COLOR=never
apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y -qq curl build-essential git sudo > /dev/null
curl -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y --default-toolchain none --profile minimal > /dev/null 2>&1
pip install -q --root-user-action=ignore uv pyyaml
export PATH=$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH RUNNER_TEMP=/tmp/runner GITHUB_WORKSPACE=/work
mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP"
git config --global --add safe.directory '*'
git clone -q /src /work
cd /work
BASE=${BASE:-$(git rev-parse HEAD~1)}
export BASE
python3 - > "$RUNNER_TEMP/steps.sh" <<'EOF'
import yaml

for s in yaml.safe_load(open(".github/workflows/benchmarks.yml"))["jobs"]["gate"]["steps"]:
    if "run" in s:
        print(f"echo; echo '=== {s.get('name', s['run'].splitlines()[0][:60])} ==='")
        print("bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail <<'STEP'\n" + s["run"].rstrip() + "\nSTEP")
EOF
bash -e "$RUNNER_TEMP/steps.sh"
echo
echo "REHEARSAL PASSED"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Check `scrutate dead` on a tree: every definition it calls dead has no whole-word occurrence of
its name outside its own lines, by ripgrep (hidden files included, the ignore files obeyed).

    python3 tools/check_dead.py BINARY [ROOT]

Prints the count and a sample; exits 1 and names each one that has an occurrence elsewhere.
"""

import json
import subprocess
import sys


def main() -> int:
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        print(__doc__.strip(), file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    binary, root = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "."
    out = subprocess.run([binary, "--root", root, "dead", "--json"], capture_output=True, text=True, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    if out.returncode not in (0, 1):
        print(out.stderr, file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    result = json.loads(out.stdout)["result"]
    bad = []
    for d in result["dead"]:
        rg = subprocess.run(
            ["rg", "--hidden", "-g", "!.git", "-g", "!.scrutate", "-n", "-w", "-F", "--no-heading", "--with-filename", "-e", d["name"], "."],
            cwd=root, capture_output=True, text=True, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
        )
        for line in rg.stdout.splitlines():
            path, num, _ = line.split(":", 2)
            path = path.removeprefix("./")
            if not (path == d["path"] and d["start"] <= int(num) <= d["end"]):
                bad.append(f"{d['id']} {d['qualname']}: {line}")
    print(f"{len(result['dead'])} dead, {len(result['undecided'])} undecided")
    for d in result["dead"][:10]:
        print(f"  {d['id']}  [{d['kind']}] {d['qualname']}")
    for b in bad:
        print(f"NAMED ELSEWHERE: {b}")
    return 1 if bad else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Fail when a release version differs from the one any shipped package declares.

usage: check_version.py VERSION   (release.yml passes the tag without its leading v)
"""
import json
import os
import re
import sys

ROOT = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "..")


# every other place a release writes its version: (file, pattern whose group 1 is the version)
WRITTEN = [
    ("integrations/vscode/package-lock.json", r'^  "version": "([^"]+)"'),
    ("integrations/vscode/package-lock.json", r'^    "": \{\n      "name": "[^"]+",\n      "version": "([^"]+)"'),
    ("packaging/scoop/scrutate.json", r'^    "version": "([^"]+)"'),
    ("packaging/scoop/scrutate.json", r"/releases/download/v([0-9][^/]*)/"),
    ("packaging/scoop/scrutate.json", r"scrutate-([0-9][^-]*)-[a-z0-9_]+-pc-windows-msvc"),
    ("packaging/homebrew/scrutate.rb", r"/refs/tags/v([^/]+)\.tar\.gz"),
    ("integrations/gitlab/.gitlab-ci.yml", r'^  SCRUTATE_VERSION: "([^"]+)"'),
    ("integrations/bitbucket/bitbucket-pipelines.yml", r"export V=(\S+)"),
    ("integrations/github/README.md", r"scrutate@v(\S+)"),
    ("integrations/github/README.md", r"version: v(\S+)"),
    ("integrations/pre-commit/README.md", r"rev: v(\S+)"),
]
WINGET = "packaging/winget/manifests/c/crisnahine/Scrutate"


def declared() -> dict[str, str]:
    out = {}
    for f in ("crates/scrutate/Cargo.toml", "crates/scrutate-py/Cargo.toml"):
        with open(os.path.join(ROOT, f)) as fh:
            # the first `version = "..."` of a manifest is the package's own
            out[f] = re.search(r'^version = "([^"]+)"', fh.read(), re.M).group(1)
    with open(os.path.join(ROOT, "integrations/vscode/package.json")) as fh:
        out["integrations/vscode/package.json"] = json.load(fh)["version"]
    for f, pattern in WRITTEN:
        with open(os.path.join(ROOT, f)) as fh:
            found = re.findall(pattern, fh.read(), re.M)
        # a pattern that finds nothing means the file changed shape: that fails too
        for i, v in enumerate(found or ["(no version found)"]):
            out[f"{f} ({pattern}, {i + 1})"] = v
    for d in sorted(os.listdir(os.path.join(ROOT, WINGET))):
        out[f"{WINGET}/{d}/"] = d
        for name in sorted(os.listdir(os.path.join(ROOT, WINGET, d))):
            with open(os.path.join(ROOT, WINGET, d, name)) as fh:
                text = fh.read()
            for i, v in enumerate(re.findall(r"^PackageVersion: (\S+)", text, re.M) + re.findall(r"/releases/download/v([0-9][^/]*)/", text)
                                  + re.findall(r"scrutate-([0-9][^-]*)-[a-z0-9_]+-pc-windows-msvc", text) or ["(no version found)"]):
                out[f"{WINGET}/{d}/{name} ({i + 1})"] = v
    return out


def main() -> int:
    want = sys.argv[1]
    bad = {f: v for f, v in declared().items() if v != want}
    for f, v in bad.items():
        print(f"{f} declares {v}, the tag says {want}")
    if not bad:
        print(f"every package declares {want}")
    return 1 if bad else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The Linux jobs of .github/workflows/ci.yml, command by command, in a clean container: the way to
# know they pass before a runner has ever seen them. It stops at the first failure.
#
#   docker run --rm -i -v "$PWD":/src:ro python:3.13-slim-bookworm bash /src/tools/ci_rehearsal.sh
#
# Not covered: the six-runner matrix (macOS, Windows), the VS Code test (it needs xvfb and a
# desktop's libraries; integrations/vscode/README.md) and anything that needs GitHub itself.
set -euo pipefail
step() { echo; echo "=== $* ==="; }
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive CARGO_TERM_COLOR=never
apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y -qq curl build-essential git ripgrep sqlite3 musl-tools file xz-utils > /dev/null
curl -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y --default-toolchain none --profile minimal > /dev/null 2>&1
export PATH=$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH
mkdir -p /work && tar -C /src --exclude=./.claude --exclude=./target --exclude=./dist --exclude=./dist-linux --exclude=node_modules --exclude=./bench/results --exclude=.vscode-test -cf - . | tar -C /work -xf -
cd /work
arch=$(uname -m)
export RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings"

step "toolchain from rust-toolchain.toml"
rustup toolchain install --no-self-update 2>&1 | tail -1
rustc --version

step "rust job: fmt, clippy, test, build, smoke"
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --exclude scrutate-py -- -D warnings 2>&1 | tail -1
cargo test --release -p scrutate --locked 2>&1 | grep -E "^test result|FAILED|panicked" | awk '/^test result/ {p+=$4; f+=$6; next} {print} END {print "tests passed:", p, "failed:", f}'
cargo build --release -p scrutate --locked 2>&1 | tail -1
./target/release/scrutate --version
./target/release/scrutate grep -F "fn main" crates/scrutate/src | head -2
./target/release/scrutate --root crates/scrutate index | tail -1
./target/release/scrutate --root crates/scrutate search "parse a file into chunks" -k 3 | head -3
./target/release/scrutate --root crates/scrutate check | tail -1

step "musl job"
rustup target add "$arch-unknown-linux-musl" 2>&1 | tail -1
cargo build --release -p scrutate --locked --target "$arch-unknown-linux-musl" 2>&1 | tail -1
m=target/$arch-unknown-linux-musl/release/scrutate
file "$m" | grep -qE "statically linked|static-pie linked"
if ldd "$m" 2>&1 | grep "=>" > /dev/null; then echo "the musl binary loads a shared library"; exit 1; fi
untimed() { sed -E 's/"elapsed_ms":[0-9.eE+-]+,?//'; }
./target/release/scrutate grep --sort --json -F "fn " crates | untimed > /tmp/glibc.jsonl
"$m" grep --sort --json -F "fn " crates | untimed > /tmp/musl.jsonl
cmp /tmp/glibc.jsonl /tmp/musl.jsonl && echo "identical: $(wc -l < /tmp/glibc.jsonl) lines"
python3 bench/musl_vs_glibc.py target/release/scrutate "$m" crates | tail -2

step "python job"
python3 --version
pip install -q --root-user-action=ignore -e "python[test]" maturin -c python/constraints.txt 2>&1 | tail -2
maturin build --release --strip -m crates/scrutate-py/Cargo.toml -o target/wheels 2>&1 | tail -1
pip install -q --root-user-action=ignore --force-reinstall --no-deps target/wheels/scrutate-*.whl
python -c "import scrutate; print(scrutate.__version__)"
(cd python && SCRUTATE_BIN=/work/target/release/scrutate python -m pytest -q -rf tests 2>&1 | tail -6)
python bench/differential.py --cases 200 --seed 3 2>&1 | tail -2
python bench/fuzz_grep.py --bin target/release/scrutate --seconds 20 --seed 7 2>&1 | tail -2
python bench/fuzz_incremental.py --bin target/release/scrutate --seconds 20 --seed 7 2>&1 | tail -2
python bench/quality.py target/release/scrutate 2>&1 | tail -1

step "compat job"
cargo test --release -p scrutate --features extra-langs --locked 2>&1 | grep -E "^test result|FAILED|panicked" | awk '/^test result/ {p+=$4; f+=$6; next} {print} END {print "tests passed:", p, "failed:", f}'
msrv=$(sed -n 's/^rust-version = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' Cargo.toml)
rustup toolchain install "$msrv" --profile minimal --no-self-update 2>&1 | tail -1
RUSTFLAGS="" cargo "+$msrv" check -p scrutate --locked 2>&1 | tail -1

step "fuzz job"
export RUSTFLAGS="" NIGHTLY=nightly-2026-10-26
rustup toolchain install "$NIGHTLY" --profile minimal --no-self-update 2>&1 | tail -1
rustc "+$NIGHTLY" --version
cargo install cargo-fuzz --version 0.13.2 --locked 2>&1 | tail -1
for f in fuzz/regressions/*/*; do
  cargo "+$NIGHTLY" fuzz run -O "$(basename "$(dirname "$f")")" "$f" 2>&1 | tail -2
done

step "editors job: Neovim"
cd /tmp
a=x86_64 sum=474430d53e6264f6d6dd18db42d6dc9df3a1b56ca9e88a325bbf860e1a811d87
[ "$arch" = aarch64 ] && a=arm64 sum=8f1f64a0bdb97247034038c3823c6cbad5bdf9ecd5751b85494b71c3ee04c815
curl -sSfL -o nvim.tar.gz "https://github.com/neovim/neovim/releases/download/v0.12.6/nvim-linux-$a.tar.gz"
echo "$sum  nvim.tar.gz" | sha256sum -c -
tar xzf nvim.tar.gz
bash /work/integrations/fixture.sh repo
cd repo
"../nvim-linux-$a/bin/nvim" --headless -u NONE -l /work/integrations/neovim/test/run.lua /work/target/release/scrutate 2>&1 | tail -4
echo
echo "REHEARSAL PASSED"

Every panel carries its own background, so one file serves GitHub's light and dark pages. Rules each SVG keeps, checked by --check: flat colour only (no gradient, no filter), no script, event handler or SMIL element, nothing loaded from outside, a title and a desc, valid XML, under 150 KB, and complete with motion off (the still state is the finished state). #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Generate docs/DEPENDENCIES.md: toolchain, direct dependencies with purpose and licence, and the size of the transitive graph, from Cargo.toml + `cargo metadata --locked`.""" from __future__ import annotations import json import os import subprocess import sys from third_party_notices import data_files # The page head (banner and navigation); tools/gen_doc_assets.py --check compares it with its table. PURPOSE = { "aho-corasick": "multi-pattern prefilter for fuzzy search", "anyhow": "error type", "blake2": "token hashing (63-bit keys)", "clap": "command-line parsing", "clap_complete": "shell completions", "flate2": "zlib for chunk text and .npz (pure Rust backend)", "grep-matcher": "matcher trait shared with grep-searcher", "grep-regex": "regex matcher with line-oriented optimisations", "grep-searcher": "buffered/mmap line searching, context, binary detection", "grep-cli": "runs the system's decompression tools for `grep -z` (bzip2, xz, zstd, lz4, brotli, .Z)", "grep-pcre2": "PCRE2 matcher for `grep -P` (look-around, backreferences)", "tar": "tar archive members for `grep -z`", "zip": "zip archive members for `grep -z` (stored and deflate)", "half": "float16 semantic model weights", "ignore": "parallel, ignore-aware directory walking (a copy in vendor/ignore; its changes are listed in the workspace Cargo.toml)", "matrixmultiply": "sgemm for k-means (pure Rust)", "memchr": "newline and NUL scans when one large file is searched in ranges", "memmap2": "memory-mapped segments", "notify": "filesystem events for `watch` and `serve --watch` (inotify, ReadDirectoryChangesW; polling on macOS)", "proptest": "property-based tests (dev only)", "pyo3": "Python bindings (optional crate)", "rayon": "data parallelism (indexing, structural search)", "regex": "identifier/heuristic patterns", "regex-syntax": "pattern syntax trees: the text index's trigram conditions and the suffix literals of a regex", "rusqlite": "SQLite (bundled)", "unicode-normalization": "NFC form of names and non-ASCII words, so two spellings of one name match", "rust-stemmers": "Snowball English stemmer", "serde": "serialisation", "serde_json": "JSON output / MCP / config", "sha1": "file content hashes", "termcolor": "coloured terminal output", "toml": "configuration files", "tree-sitter": "incremental parsing runtime", } def main() -> int: meta = json.loads(subprocess.run(["cargo", "metadata", "--format-version", "1", "--locked"], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout) pkgs = {p["id"]: p for p in meta["packages"]} core = next(p for p in meta["packages"] if p["name"] == "scrutate") nodes = {n["id"]: n for n in meta["resolve"]["nodes"]} # transitive normal+build deps of the core seen, stack = set(), [core["id"]] while stack: nid = stack.pop() if nid in seen: continue seen.add(nid) for dep in nodes[nid]["deps"]: if any(k["kind"] in (None, "build") for k in dep["dep_kinds"]): stack.append(dep["pkg"]) shipped = len(seen) - 1 rustc = subprocess.run(["rustc", "--version"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip() out = [DOC_HEAD, f"Generated by `tools/gen_dependencies_md.py` from `Cargo.toml` and `cargo metadata --locked`.\n", "## Toolchain\n", f"- Built and tested with `{rustc}` (pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml`); minimum supported `rust-version` = {core['rust_version']}.", "- Edition 2021. Release profile: `opt-level=3`, fat LTO, `codegen-units=1`, no debug info, stripped.", "- Python ≥ 3.9 is needed only for the optional bindings, the training code of the models and the benchmark/test harnesses.\n", "## Direct dependencies of the `scrutate` crate\n", "| Crate | Version (locked) | Licence | Purpose | Optional |", "|---|---|---|---|---|"] # one row per crate: a crate declared twice (per target, with other features) is one dependency direct = sorted({d["name"]: d for d in core["dependencies"]}.values(), key=lambda d: d["name"]) grammars = [] for d in direct: if d["kind"] == "dev": continue locked = next((p for p in meta["packages"] if p["name"] == d["name"]), None) ver = locked["version"] if locked else d["req"] lic = (locked or {}).get("license") or "?" if d["name"].startswith("tree-sitter-"): grammars.append((d["name"], ver, lic, d["optional"])) continue out.append(f"| {d['name']} | {ver} | {lic} | {PURPOSE.get(d['name'], '')} | {'yes' if d['optional'] else ''} |") out.append(f"\n{len(grammars)} tree-sitter grammar crates ({sum(1 for g in grammars if not g[3])} default, {sum(1 for g in grammars if g[3])} behind `extra-langs`):\n") out.append("| Grammar crate | Version | Licence | Optional |") out.append("|---|---|---|---|") for n, v, l, o in grammars: out.append(f"| {n} | {v} | {l} | {'yes' if o else ''} |") out.append("\n## Data compiled into the binary\n") out.append("| Data | Version | Licence | Source | Purpose |") out.append("|---|---|---|---|---|") for d in data_files(): out.append(f"| `{d['file']}` | Unicode {d['version']} | {d['license']} | {d['url']} | {d['purpose']} |") out.append(f"\n## Transitive graph\n\n{shipped} crates are compiled into the release binary (normal + build dependencies, dev dependencies excluded); " "the exact set with licences and purls is the SBOM produced by `tools/sbom.py` (CycloneDX 1.5). `cargo audit` result: see docs/TEST_RESULTS.md.\n") out.append("## Policy\n") out.append("- A dependency is added only with a written reason (what it replaces, size, maintenance, licence) and must be permissively licensed.\n" "- `Cargo.lock` is committed; CI builds with `--locked`; `cargo audit` runs on every push and the SBOM is attached to every release.\n" "- C code in the dependency tree: SQLite (bundled), tree-sitter runtime and grammars. No other native code; no networking crates.\n") with open(os.path.join(ROOT, "docs", "DEPENDENCIES.md"), "w") as f: f.write("\n".join(out) + "\n") print(f"wrote docs/DEPENDENCIES.md ({shipped} shipped crates)", file=sys.stderr) return 0 if __name__ == "__main__": sys.exit(main())

def spans(text):
    """Split `code` marks: a list of (text, is_code)."""
    parts = text.split("`")
    return [(p, i % 2 == 1) for i, p in enumerate(parts) if p]


def text_width(text, size):
    # Generous per-character widths, so a wider fallback font still fits.
    return sum(len(t) * (0.61 if code else 0.53) * size for t, code in spans(text))


def wrap(text, width, size):
    """Greedy wrap at spaces outside code marks; every line fits width with 10% to spare."""
    words, cur, inside = [], "", False
    for ch in text:
        if ch == "`":
            inside = not inside
        if ch == " " and not inside:
            words.append(cur)
            cur = ""
        else:
            cur += ch
    words.append(cur)
    lines, line = [], ""
    for w in words:
        cand = (line + " " + w) if line else w
        if text_width(cand, size) <= width * 0.9 or not line:
            line = cand
        else:
            lines.append(line)
            line = w
    lines.append(line)
    for ln in lines:
        if text_width(ln, size) > width * 0.9:
            raise SystemExit(f"text does not fit {width}px at {size}px: {ln!r}")
    return lines


def rich(x, y, text, cls, anchor=None):
    out = [f'<text x="{x:g}" y="{y:g}" class="{cls}"' + (f' text-anchor="{anchor}"' if anchor else "") + ">"]
    for t, code in spans(text):
        out.append(f'<tspan class="m">{escape(t)}</tspan>' if code else escape(t))
    out.append("</text>")
    return "".join(out)


STYLE = f"""
text {{ font-family: {SANS}; }}
.m {{ font-family: {MONO}; }}
.pre {{ white-space: pre; }}
.h {{ font-size: 15px; font-weight: 700; fill: @fg@; }}
.hm {{ font-size: 15px; font-weight: 700; fill: {INK}; }}
.b {{ font-size: 14px; fill: @dim@; }}
.bi {{ font-size: 14px; fill: @fg@; }}
.b .m, .bi .m {{ fill: @fg@; }}
.lbl {{ font-family: {MONO}; font-size: 11.5px; letter-spacing: 1.6px; fill: @dim@; }}
.card, .inset {{ fill: @bg@; stroke: @rule@; stroke-width: 1; }}
.store {{ fill: @bg@; stroke: @fg@; stroke-width: 1.25; }}
.out {{ fill: @bg@; stroke: @fg@; stroke-width: 1.5; }}
.arrow {{ fill: none; stroke: @dim@; stroke-width: 1.5; stroke-linecap: round; stroke-linejoin: round; }}
.gate {{ fill: @bg@; stroke: @dim@; stroke-width: 1.25; stroke-dasharray: 6 5; }}
"""

# A diagram's loop: a block of the highlighter runs along each arrow in the order data flows, the card the
# flow ends in is marked when the last block arrives, it holds, the mark lifts and the flow starts again.
TRAVEL, HOLD = 1.1, 2.6

R_CARD = 4          # corner of a card inside a diagram
MARGIN, TOP = 32, 72  # where a diagram's drawing sits inside its panel, under its label


def tokens(on):
    c = ON[on]
    return {"fg": c["fg"], "dim": c["dim"], "rule": c["rule"], "bg": c["bg"], "mark": MARK, "alert": ALERT, "ink": INK}


def fill(src, on):
    t = tokens(on)
    out = re.sub(r"@(\w+)@", lambda m: t[m.group(1)], src)
    if re.search(r"@\w+@", out):
        raise SystemExit("unfilled colour token")
    return out


def document(w, h, title, desc, body, style):
    animated = "@keyframes" in style
    return (f'<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 {w} {h}" width="{w}" height="{h}" role="img" '
            f'aria-labelledby="t d">\n{WRITTEN}\n<title id="t">{escape(title)}</title>\n<desc id="d">{escape(desc)}</desc>\n'
            f"<style>{style}{REDUCED + chr(10) if animated else ''}</style>\n{body}\n</svg>\n")


def outlined(text):
    """True when the headline font has every letter of `text` in capitals."""
    return "`" not in text and all(ch == " " or ch in G.font()["glyphs"] for ch in text.upper())


def lbl(x, y, text, anchor=None):
    """A small label in spaced mono capitals."""
    return f'<text x="{x:g}" y="{y:g}" class="lbl"' + (f' text-anchor="{anchor}"' if anchor else "") + f">{escape(text.upper())}</text>"


class Svg:
    def __init__(self, w, h, title, desc, on="ink"):
        self.w, self.h, self.title, self.desc, self.on = w, h, title, desc, on
        self.body, self.style, self.defs, self.flows, self.moves = [], [STYLE], [], [], {}
        self.lead = 0.6   # when the flow has arrived, for a diagram whose own motion takes longer

    def add(self, s):
        self.body.append(s)

    def move(self, name, fn):
        """An element of its own motion: its class is `@m:name@`, filled by fn(clock, the time the flow
        arrives, the loop's length) once the loop is known."""
        self.moves[name] = fn
        return f"@m:{name}@"

    def heading(self, x, y, text, marked=False, mono_title=False, room=None):
        """A card's title at baseline y: outlined capitals, or bold system text when it holds code.
        `marked` puts it on a highlighter slab that wipes in when the last block arrives."""
        cap = 11 if room is None else min(11, room / G.type_w(text.upper(), 1))   # a long title is set a little smaller
        plain = not mono_title and outlined(text) and cap >= 9.5
        t = f"`{text}`" if mono_title else text
        if plain:
            w, top, h = G.type_w(text.upper(), cap), y - cap - 6, cap + 12
        else:
            w, top, h = text_width(t, 15) * 0.93, y - 16, 22
        if marked:
            self.add(G.marker(x - 7, top, w + 14, h, "wipe @cls:slab@"))
        # a marked title is drawn twice: in the panel's colour, and in ink over it while the slab is there
        if plain:
            self.add(G.words(text.upper(), x, y, cap, "@fg@"))
            if marked:
                self.add(G.words(text.upper(), x, y, cap, INK, cls="@cls:ink@"))
        else:
            self.add(rich(x, y, t, "h"))
            if marked:
                self.add(rich(x, y, t, "hm @cls:ink@"))

    def box(self, x, y, w, h, cls):
        if cls == "store":   # a store has its top right corner cut, like the README's cards
            k = 12
            self.add(f'<path d="M{x:g} {y:g} H{x + w - k:g} L{x + w:g} {y + k:g} V{y + h:g} H{x:g} Z" class="store"/>')
        else:
            self.add(f'<rect x="{x:g}" y="{y:g}" width="{w:g}" height="{h:g}" rx="{R_CARD}" class="{cls}"/>')

    def card(self, x, y, w, title, text, cls="card", h=None, title_mono=False, marked=None):
        """A card with a title and wrapped body paragraphs; returns its height. An `out` card is marked."""
        lines = []
        for para in ([text] if isinstance(text, str) else text):
            lines += wrap(para, w - 32, 14)
        need = 30 + 20 * len(lines) + 12 if title else 14 + 20 * len(lines) + 4
        h = h or need
        if h < need:
            raise SystemExit(f"card {title!r} needs {need}px, has {h}")
        self.box(x, y, w, h, cls)
        ty = y + 26
        if title:
            self.heading(x + 16, y + 27, title, marked=(cls == "out") if marked is None else marked,
                         mono_title=title_mono, room=w - 32)
            ty += 22
        else:
            ty = y + 24
        for ln in lines:
            self.add(rich(x + 16, ty, ln, "b"))
            ty += 20
        return h

    @staticmethod
    def need(w, title, text):
        n = sum(len(wrap(p, w - 32, 14)) for p in ([text] if isinstance(text, str) else text))
        return 30 + 20 * n + 12

    def arrow(self, pts, flow=None, head=True, both=False):
        d = "M" + " L".join(f"{x:g} {y:g}" for x, y in pts)
        marks = (' marker-end="url(#ah)"' if head else "") + (' marker-start="url(#ah)"' if both else "")
        self.add(f'<path d="{d}" class="arrow"{marks}/>')
        if flow is not None:
            length = sum(abs(x1 - x0) + abs(y1 - y0) for (x0, y0), (x1, y1) in zip(pts, pts[1:]))
            dash = min(30.0, 10 / length * 100)  # a 10 px block, whatever the arrow's length
            self.flows.append((flow, dash))
            self.add(G.dash_path(d, f"@flow{len(self.flows)}@", f"{dash:.1f} 300", 9).replace(MARK, "@mark@"))

    def svg(self):
        """The drawing, scaled into a panel under a `// TITLE` label, with its loop."""
        clk = G.Clock()
        arrive = max([f + TRAVEL for f, _ in self.flows] + [self.lead])
        clk.total = round(arrive + 0.35 + HOLD + 0.7, 2)
        T = clk.total
        inner = "\n".join(self.body)
        for n, (flow, dash) in enumerate(self.flows, 1):
            inner = inner.replace(f"@flow{n}@", G.dash_run(clk, flow, flow + TRAVEL, dash=dash)[0])
        if self.flows:
            clk.beat("a block of highlighter runs along each arrow, in the order data flows", 0, arrive)
        if "@cls:slab@" in inner:
            inner = inner.replace("@cls:slab@", clk.anim(G.wipe(arrive, 0.32) + [(T - 0.6, "scaleX(1)", "ease-in"), (T - 0.3, "scaleX(0)")],
                                                   rest="scaleX(0)"))
            inner = inner.replace("@cls:ink@", clk.anim([(arrive + 0.2, 0, "steps(1, end)"), (arrive + 0.21, 1),
                                                   (T - 0.6, 1, "steps(1, end)"), (T - 0.59, 0)], "opacity", rest=0))
            clk.beat("the card the flow ends in is marked", arrive, 0.35)
        for name, fn in self.moves.items():
            inner = inner.replace(f"@m:{name}@", fn(clk, arrive, T))
        clk.beat("hold, then the marks lift", arrive + 0.35, T - arrive - 0.35)
        if clk.tracks:
            self.style.append("\n" + G.WIPE_CSS + "\n" + G.SPOT_CSS + "\n" + clk.css() + "\n")
        sc = (W - 2 * MARGIN) / self.w
        H = round(TOP + self.h * sc + 30)
        head = ('<marker id="ah" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="8.5" refY="5" markerWidth="6.5" markerHeight="6.5" '
                'orient="auto-start-reverse"><path d="M1.5 1.5 8.5 5 1.5 8.5" fill="none" stroke="@dim@" '
                'stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/></marker>')
        body = "\n".join([
            G.panel(H, self.on, dots=self.on == "ink"),
            G.label(MARGIN + 8, 46, "", self.title, self.on, W - MARGIN - 8),
            "<defs>" + head + "".join(self.defs) + "</defs>",
            f'<g transform="translate({MARGIN} {TOP}) scale({sc:.5f})">',
            inner,
            "</g>",
        ])
        src = document(W, H, self.title, self.desc, body, "".join(self.style))
        return fill(src, self.on)


def marked_at(t):
    """A slab of a diagram's own that wipes in at t and lifts with the loop's other marks."""
    return lambda clk, arrive, T: "wipe " + clk.anim(G.wipe(t, 0.3) + [(T - 0.6, "scaleX(1)", "ease-in"), (T - 0.3, "scaleX(0)")],
                                                     rest="scaleX(0)")


def hops(stops, t0, step):
    """A reticle that appears on the first of `stops`, settles on each in turn, rests on the last and goes."""
    def fn(clk, arrive, T):
        def at(p, s, o=1):
            return {"transform": f"translate({p[0]:g}px, {p[1]:g}px) scale({s})", "opacity": o}
        pts = [(t0 - 0.2, at(stops[0], 1.7, 0), G.EASE), (t0 + 0.2, at(stops[0], 1))]
        for k, p in enumerate(stops[1:], 1):
            t = t0 + step * k
            pts += [(t - 0.28, at(stops[k - 1], 1), G.EASE_IN_OUT), (t, at(p, 1.25), G.EASE), (t + 0.14, at(p, 1))]
        pts += [(T - 0.6, at(stops[-1], 1), "ease-in"), (T - 0.3, at(stops[-1], 1.4, 0))]
        return clk.anim(pts, rest=at(stops[-1], 1.4, 0), travel=True)
    return fn


def reticle_box(cls, w, h, colour="@fg@"):
    """Corner ticks round a w by h box centred on 0 0; hidden until its motion shows it."""
    return f'<g class="{cls}" opacity="0">' + G.ticks(-w / 2, -h / 2, w, h, colour, n=min(10, w / 3)) + "</g>"


def icon_paths(name, stroke, width=1.75):
    return "".join(f'<path d="{d}" fill="none" stroke="{stroke}" stroke-width="{width}" '
                   'stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/>' for d in ICONS[name])


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- banners, group strips and icons

def group_no(g):
    return f"{[k for k, _, _ in GROUPS].index(g) + 1:02d}"


def banner(key, title, line, icon, group=None):
    """A document's banner: its group label, its title in outlined capitals with a highlighter cursor, the
    question it answers and its icon. The hub's banner (no group) is taller."""
    on = GROUP_ON[group] if group else "ink"
    c = ON[on]
    hub_banner = group is None
    H = 168 if hub_banner else 150
    b = [G.panel(H, on)]
    if hub_banner:
        tag_text = "SCRUTATE // DOCS"
        tw = G.text_w(tag_text, 11, True, 0.14) + 18
        b.append(G.label(PAD, 44, "", f"{len(DOCS)} documents // {len(GROUPS)} groups", on, W - PAD - tw - 16))
        b.append(G.tag(W - PAD - tw, 30, tag_text, on)[0])
    else:
        b.append(G.label(PAD, 44, group_no(group), next(n for g, n, _ in GROUPS if g == group), on, W - PAD))
    t = title.upper()
    room = W - 2 * PAD - 110
    cap = min(46 if hub_banner else 34, room / (G.type_w(t, 1) + 0.8))
    base = 114 if hub_banner else 98
    b.append(G.words(t, PAD, base, cap, c["fg"]))
    cx = PAD + G.type_w(t, cap) + cap * 0.2
    # the loop: the reticle round the icon closes on it and settles, holds, and lets go; the cursor blinks
    clk = G.Clock(5.2)
    edge = f' stroke="{INK}" stroke-width="1.5"' if on == "paper" else ""   # on paper an ink edge keeps the highlighter visible
    b.append(f'<rect class="{G.blink(clk, 0, clk.total, clk.total / 5)}" x="{cx:.1f}" y="{base - cap:.1f}" '
             f'width="{cap * 0.58:.1f}" height="{cap:.1f}" fill="{MARK}"{edge}/>')
    if text_width(line, 15) > room:
        raise SystemExit(f"banner line too long: {key}")
    b.append(rich(PAD, base + 31, line, "q"))
    s = 60
    ix, iy = W - PAD - s, (H - s) / 2 + 12
    settle = clk.anim([(0.4, {"transform": "scale(1.45)", "opacity": 0}, G.EASE), (0.95, {"transform": "scale(1)", "opacity": 1}),
                       (4.5, {"transform": "scale(1)", "opacity": 1}, "ease-in"), (4.9, {"transform": "scale(1.2)", "opacity": 0})],
                      rest={"transform": "scale(1.2)", "opacity": 0}, travel=True)
    clk.beat("the reticle closes on the icon and settles", 0.4, 0.55)
    clk.beat("it holds, then lets go; the cursor blinks throughout", 0.95, 3.95)
    b.append(f'<g class="{settle} spot">' + G.ticks(ix, iy, s, s, c["dim"]) + "</g>")
    k = 1.9
    b.append(f'<g transform="translate({ix + (s - 24 * k) / 2:.1f} {iy + (s - 24 * k) / 2:.1f}) scale({k})">{icon_paths(icon, c["fg"])}</g>')
    style = (f"\n.m {{ font-family: {MONO}; }} .pre {{ white-space: pre; }}\n"
             f"text {{ font-family: {SANS}; }} .q {{ font-size: 15px; fill: {c['dim']}; }}\n"
             + G.SPOT_CSS + "\n" + clk.css() + "\n")
    return document(W, H, f"{title}: scrutate documentation", f"Banner for the {title} page. {line}", "\n".join(b), style)


def group_strip(g, name):
    """The band before each group on the hub: `// 01  USE IT`."""
    on = GROUP_ON[g]
    c = ON[on]
    H, n = 84, group_no(g)
    b = [G.panel(H, on, frame=False), G.words("//", PAD, 56, 26, c["dim"]), G.words(n, PAD + 58, 56, 26, c["fg"])]
    x = PAD + 58 + G.type_w(n, 26) + 26
    b.append(G.words(name.upper(), x, 53, 19, c["fg"]))
    end = x + G.type_w(name.upper(), 19) + 22
    b.append(f'<path d="M{end:.1f} 44 H{W - PAD - 34}" stroke="{c["rule"]}"/>')
    clk = G.Clock(4.8)
    b.append(G.seek(clk, end, W - PAD - 24, 44, W - PAD - 12, 8, c["dim"], t0=0.3 + 0.3 * (int(n) % 3), on=on))
    style = "\n" + G.SPOT_CSS + "\n" + clk.css() + "\n"
    return document(W, H, f"{n}: {name}", f"Group {n} of the documentation hub: {name.lower()}.", "\n".join(b), style)


def icon_svg(name, title):
    """An ink chip with the icon in paper strokes, as the README's icons: one file reads on both page colours."""
    body = (f'<rect width="32" height="32" rx="6" fill="{INK}"/><g transform="translate(5 5) scale(.9167)">'
            f'{icon_paths(name, PAPER, 1.9)}</g>')
    return document(32, 32, title, f"Icon for {title}.", body, "")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- diagrams

def diagram_engine_a():
    s = Svg(880, 510, "Engine A: from the command line to output",
            "The command line is parsed, the ignore-aware parallel walker visits the files, each file's first read "
            "decides its path (small file, stream reader, split file, long lines), and the output is batched per file.")
    w3, top = 262, 1
    cards = [
        ("Command line", ["`scrutate grep PATTERN`", "Arguments of the plain shapes are read by hand, anything else by clap."]),
        ("Walk", ["The `ignore` parallel walker: `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, global excludes; hidden files off.",
                  "Threads: the cores (at most 12); on macOS the performance cores; more when files come from the disk."]),
        ("First read of a file", ["64 KB and one byte. A NUL byte or a byte-order mark sends the file to the stream reader."]),
    ]
    h1 = max(Svg.need(w3, t, b) for t, b in cards)
    xs = [1, 309, 617]
    for x, (t, b) in zip(xs, cards):
        s.card(x, top, w3, t, b, h=h1)
    my = top + h1 / 2
    s.arrow([(xs[0] + w3 + 2, my), (xs[1] - 4, my)], flow=0)
    s.arrow([(xs[1] + w3 + 2, my), (xs[2] - 4, my)], flow=1.2)
    paths = [
        ("Small file", "A short first read is the whole file: searched in the thread's own buffer."),
        ("Larger file", "The stream reader, up to 1 MB with a searcher made for that file."),
        ("Split file", "Ranges of whole lines (8 MB each); one window of ranges per thread."),
        ("One long line", "No line break before the last byte: a plain -F literal reads it in two passes through small buffers; else one buffer of the file's size."),
    ]
    w4, y2 = 206, top + h1 + 84
    h2 = max(Svg.need(w4, t, b) for t, b in paths)
    px = [1, 225, 449, 673]
    for x, (t, b) in zip(px, paths):
        s.card(x, y2, w4, t, b, h=h2)
    # bracket over the two paths for files of 64 MB or more
    by = y2 - 12
    s.add(f'<path d="M{px[2] + 8} {by + 6} V{by} H{px[3] + w4 - 8} V{by + 6}" fill="none" stroke="@rule@" stroke-width="1.5"/>')
    s.add(lbl((px[2] + px[3] + w4) / 2, by - 8, "64 MB or more", "middle"))
    bus = top + h1 + 26
    cx3 = xs[2] + w3 / 2
    s.arrow([(cx3, top + h1 + 2), (cx3, bus)], head=False, flow=2.4)
    s.add(f'<path d="M{px[0] + w4 / 2} {bus} H{px[3] + w4 / 2}" class="arrow"/>')
    for i, x in enumerate(px):
        c = x + w4 / 2
        s.arrow([(c, bus), (c, y2 - 4)], flow=3.4)
    y3 = y2 + h2 + 50
    out = ["Matches are batched per file and sent to the caller's sink while other threads keep searching; "
           "plain piped output shares one 64 KB buffer, so the lines of many files leave in one write.",
           "Ctrl-C, `--max-results` or a closed pipe cancels the walk between files. `--sort` gives path order."]
    h3 = s.card(1, y3, 878, "Output", out, cls="out")
    for x in px:
        c = x + w4 / 2
        s.arrow([(c, y2 + h2 + 2), (c, y3 - 4)], flow=4.6)
    s.h = int(y3 + h3 + 2)
    return s


def diagram_engine_b():
    s = Svg(880, 560, "Engine B: one index update",
            "Walk, hash, parse and chunk the files; the chunks give rows for SQLite (symbols, call edges, imports) "
            "and arrays for a new segment (BM25 postings, int8 vectors); one transaction commits both.")
    w, xs = 194, [1, 229, 457, 685]
    row1 = [
        ("Walk", "Files the ignore rules let through; binary files and files over 1 MB are left out."),
        ("Hash", "Size, mtime and `ctime_ns` match: the fast path. Otherwise a SHA-1 of the content."),
        ("Parse", "Tree-sitter rules, a keyword heuristic, or line windows."),
        ("Chunks", "One per definition; every other line in overlapping 50-line windows."),
    ]
    h1 = max(Svg.need(w, t, b) for t, b in row1)
    for x, (t, b) in zip(xs, row1):
        s.card(x, 1, w, t, b, h=h1)
    my = 1 + h1 / 2
    for i in range(3):
        s.arrow([(xs[i] + w + 2, my), (xs[i + 1] - 4, my)], flow=i * 0.9)
    w2, x2 = 270, [1, 304, 607]
    row2 = [
        ("Symbols and call edges", "Chunk metadata and text, call edges (`refs`) and `imports`."),
        ("BM25 postings", "Per field, over a shared 63-bit token-hash vocabulary."),
        ("Vectors", "int8, two views per chunk (description, implementation); IVF cluster order from 20,000 rows."),
    ]
    y2 = 1 + h1 + 72
    h2 = max(Svg.need(w2, t, b) for t, b in row2)
    for x, (t, b) in zip(x2, row2):
        s.card(x, y2, w2, t, b, h=h2)
    bus = 1 + h1 + 34
    cx = xs[3] + w / 2
    s.arrow([(cx, 1 + h1 + 2), (cx, bus)], head=False, flow=2.7)
    s.add(f'<path d="M{x2[0] + w2 / 2} {bus} H{cx}" class="arrow"/>')
    for x in x2:
        s.arrow([(x + w2 / 2, bus), (x + w2 / 2, y2 - 4)], flow=3.6)
    y3 = y2 + h2 + 60
    sql = ["`files`, `chunks`, `refs`, `imports`, `meta` (with the segment manifest); WAL.",
           "One `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction per update: readers never see a half state."]
    seg = ["`.scrutate/seg/sNNNNNN/`: immutable, memory-mapped `.npy` arrays.",
           "Written to a temporary directory, then renamed."]
    h3 = s.card(1, y3, w2, "SQLite `index.db`", sql, cls="store")
    hs = s.card(304, y3, 573, "Segment", seg, cls="store")
    s.arrow([(x2[0] + w2 / 2, y2 + h2 + 2), (x2[0] + w2 / 2, y3 - 4)], flow=4.5)
    for x in x2[1:]:
        s.arrow([(x + w2 / 2, y2 + h2 + 2), (x + w2 / 2, y3 - 4)], flow=4.5)
    ay = y3 + hs / 2
    s.arrow([(302, ay), (x2[0] + w2 + 4, ay)], flow=5.4)
    s.h = int(y3 + h3 + 2)

def rel(frm, to):
    return os.path.relpath(os.path.join(ROOT, to), os.path.dirname(os.path.join(ROOT, frm))).replace(os.sep, "/")


def headed():
    return [d for d in DOCS if not d[0].startswith("+")]


def strip_code(md):
    """Lines outside fenced code blocks, with their numbers."""
    out, fence = [], None
    for i, ln in enumerate(md.split("\n")):
        m = re.match(r"^\s*(```+|~~~+)", ln)
        if m:
            if fence is None:
                fence = m.group(1)[0] * 3
            elif ln.strip().startswith(fence):
                fence = None
            continue
        if fence is None:
            out.append((i, ln))
    return out


def slug(heading):
    t = re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", heading).strip().lower()
    t = re.sub(r"\[([^\]]*)\]\([^)]*\)", r"\1", t)
    t = re.sub(r"[^\w\- ]", "", t, flags=re.UNICODE)
    return t.replace(" ", "-")


def headings(md):
    seen, out = {}, []
    for _, ln in strip_code(md):
        m = re.match(r"^(#{1,6})\s+(.*?)\s*#*\s*$", ln)
        if m:
            base = slug(m.group(2))
            n = seen.get(base, 0)
            seen[base] = n + 1
            out.append((len(m.group(1)), m.group(2), base if n == 0 else f"{base}-{n}"))
    return out


def banner_block(path, key, title, line):
    a = rel(path, "docs/assets")
    return ["<p align=\"center\">",
            f"<img src=\"{a}/banner-{key}.svg\" alt=\"{escape(title)}. {escape(line)}\" width=\"880\">",
            "</p>"]


def nav_line(doc):
    key, path, *_ = doc
    group = [d for d in headed() if d[5] == doc[5]]
    i = [d[0] for d in group].index(key)
    parts = [f"[Documentation]({rel(path, HUB)})"]
    if i > 0:
        p = group[i - 1]
        parts.append(f"Previous: [{p[2]}]({rel(path, p[1])})")
    if i + 1 < len(group):
        n = group[i + 1]
        parts.append(f"Next: [{n[2]}]({rel(path, n[1])})")
    return "  ·  ".join(parts)


def toc_label(heading):
    # A heading's trailing file list, "(`ops.rs`, ...)", is left out of the contents line.
    return re.sub(r"\s*\([^)]*`[^)]*\)\s*$", "", heading).replace("`", "")


def head(doc, h1, body):
    key, path, title, line, icon, group, toc = doc
    out = [HEAD_START] + banner_block(path, key, title, line) + ["", h1, "", nav_line(doc)]
    if toc:
        hs = [(t, a) for lvl, t, a in headings(h1 + "\n" + body) if lvl == 2]
        out += ["", "**Contents**: " + "  ·  ".join(f"[{toc_label(t)}](#{a})" for t, a in hs)]
    out += ["", HEAD_END]
    return "\n".join(out) + "\n"


def split_doc(text):
    """(h1, body) of a document with or without a head."""
    if text.startswith(HEAD_START):
        end = text.index(HEAD_END) + len(HEAD_END) + 1
        h1 = next(ln for ln in text[:end].split("\n") if ln.startswith("# "))
        return h1, text[end:]
    first, _, rest = text.partition("\n")
    if not first.startswith("# "):
        raise SystemExit("a document must start with its # title")
    return first, rest


def with_head(doc, text):
    h1, body = split_doc(text)
    return head(doc, h1, body) + body


def hub():
    out = [HEAD_START] + banner_block(HUB, "docs", "Documentation", "Every document, grouped by what you came to do") + [
        "", "# Documentation", "",
        "The documents are grouped by what you came to do: use scrutate, understand how it works, check the "
        "evidence behind its claims, or work on it. Each document starts with a link back here and to the "
        "documents before and after it in its group. A document written by a script says so at the top; "
        "change the script, not the page.",
        "", HEAD_END, "", "<table>"]
    # One table, so the columns line up from group to group; each group opens with its band.
    for g, name, line in GROUPS:
        out += ["<tr>", f'<th colspan="2" align="left"><img src="assets/banner-group-{g}.svg" width="100%" '
                f'alt="{group_no(g)} {escape(name)}"><br><sub>{escape(line)}</sub></th>', "</tr>"]
        docs = [d for d in DOCS if d[5] == g]
        for i in range(0, len(docs), 2):
            out.append("<tr>")
            for d in docs[i:i + 2]:
                key, path, title, q, icon = d[:5]
                ikey = key.lstrip("+")
                out += ['<td width="50%" valign="top">',
                        f'<img src="assets/banner-icon-{ikey}.svg" width="20" height="20" alt=""> '
                        f'<a href="{rel(HUB, path)}"><b>{escape(title)}</b></a><br>',
                        escape(q),
                        "</td>"]
            if len(docs[i:i + 2]) == 1:
                out.append('<td width="50%"></td>')
            out.append("</tr>")
    out += ["</table>", ""]
    return "\n".join(out)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- writing and checking

def planned():
    """Every file this script owns, path -> content."""
    files = {}
    for d in DOCS:
        key, path, title, line, icon = d[:5]
        k = key.lstrip("+")
        files[f"docs/assets/banner-icon-{k}.svg"] = icon_svg(icon, title)
        if not key.startswith("+"):
            files[f"docs/assets/banner-{k}.svg"] = banner(k, title, line, icon, d[5])
    files["docs/assets/banner-docs.svg"] = banner("docs", "Documentation", "Every document, grouped by what you came to do", "docs")
    for g, name, _ in GROUPS:
        files[f"docs/assets/banner-group-{g}.svg"] = group_strip(g, name)
    for name, fn in DIAGRAMS.items():
        files[f"docs/assets/diagram-{name}.svg"] = fn().svg()
    files[HUB] = hub()
    for d in headed():
        if d[1] in GENERATORS:
            continue
        with open(os.path.join(ROOT, d[1]), encoding="utf-8") as f:
            files[d[1]] = with_head(d, f.read())
    return files


def generator_head(gen):
    with open(os.path.join(ROOT, gen), encoding="utf-8") as f:
        tree = ast.parse(f.read())
    for node in tree.body:
        if isinstance(node, ast.Assign) and any(getattr(t, "id", "") == "DOC_HEAD" for t in node.targets):
            return ast.literal_eval(node.value)
    return None


def check_svg(path, txt, problems):
    """The README's image rules (gen_assets.svg_problems): valid XML, a title and a desc, under 150 KB,
    no gradient, filter, script or outside reference, and a reduced-motion rule wherever there is motion."""
    problems += G.svg_problems(path, txt)


def check_links(path, text, problems):
    base = os.path.dirname(os.path.join(ROOT, path))
    own = {a for _, _, a in headings(text)}
    for n, ln in strip_code(text):
        ln = re.sub(r"`[^`]*`", "", ln)
        targets = re.findall(r"\]\(([^)\s]+)\)", ln) + re.findall(r"""(?:href|src|srcset)=["']([^"']+)["']""", ln)
        for t in targets:
            if re.match(r"^[a-z]+:", t):
                continue
            file, _, anchor = t.partition("#")
            if file:
                full = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(base, file))
                if not os.path.exists(full):
                    problems.append(f"{path}:{n + 1}: {t}: no such file")
                    continue
                if anchor:
                    if not full.endswith(".md"):
                        continue
                    with open(full, encoding="utf-8") as f:
                        anchors = {a for _, _, a in headings(f.read())}
                    if anchor not in anchors:
                        problems.append(f"{path}:{n + 1}: {t}: no such heading")
            elif anchor and anchor not in own:
                problems.append(f"{path}:{n + 1}: #{anchor}: no such heading")


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--check", action="store_true", help="change nothing; fail when a file differs or a link is broken")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    files = planned()
    problems = []
    for path, txt in sorted(files.items()):
        full = os.path.join(ROOT, path)
        if path.endswith(".svg"):
            check_svg(path, txt, problems)
        try:
            with open(full, encoding="utf-8") as f:
                cur = f.read()
        except FileNotFoundError:
            cur = None
        if cur != txt:
            if a.check:
                problems.append(f"{path}: differs from what tools/gen_doc_assets.py writes")
            else:
                os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(full), exist_ok=True)
                with open(full, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                    f.write(txt)
                print(f"wrote {path}", file=sys.stderr)
    owned = {os.path.basename(p) for p in files if p.startswith("docs/assets/")}
    for name in sorted(os.listdir(ASSETS)):
        if name.startswith(("banner-", "diagram-")) and name not in owned:
            problems.append(f"docs/assets/{name}: not written by this script (remove it)")
    for doc_path, gen in GENERATORS.items():
        d = next(x for x in DOCS if x[1] == doc_path)
        with open(os.path.join(ROOT, doc_path), encoding="utf-8") as f:
            text = f.read()
        h1, body = split_doc(text)
        want = head(d, h1, body)
        if generator_head(gen) != want:
            problems.append(f"{gen}: DOC_HEAD differs from the head of {doc_path} this script would write")
        if not text.startswith(want):
            problems.append(f"{doc_path}: its head differs from the one {gen} writes")
    listed = {d[1] for d in DOCS}
    for name in sorted(os.listdir(os.path.join(ROOT, "docs"))):
        p = f"docs/{name}"
        if (name.endswith(".md") or name.endswith(".html")) and p not in listed and p != HUB:
            problems.append(f"{p}: not on the hub (add it to DOCS)")
    for path in [HUB] + [d[1] for d in headed()]:
        text = files.get(path)
        if text is None:
            with open(os.path.join(ROOT, path), encoding="utf-8") as f:
                text = f.read()
        check_links(path, text, problems)
    for p in problems:
        print(p, file=sys.stderr)
    if problems:
        return 1
    print(f"{len(files)} files {'checked' if a.check else 'up to date'}; links and anchors resolve", file=sys.stderr)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate crates/scrutate/data/han_fold.txt, the traditional-to-simplified Han fold of ranked search.

Reads `Unihan_Variants.txt` (inside https://www.unicode.org/Public/UCD/latest/ucd/Unihan.zip) and
keeps one pair per character whose `kSimplifiedVariant` differs from itself: the first listed value
that is not the character. A target that is itself folded is followed to the end of its chain, so
folding twice gives the same result as folding once. A pair is kept only when both characters are in
the scripts the engine cuts into pairs (`unspaced`), the only place the fold applies. The engine
embeds the output file.

usage: gen_han_fold.py PATH/TO/Unihan_Variants.txt
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import re
import sys


def unspaced(c: str) -> bool:
    """Scripts written without spaces between words, as the engine's text.rs lists them: Han,
    Hiragana, Katakana, and Thai, Lao, Tibetan, Myanmar, Khmer, the Tai scripts, Balinese and Javanese."""
    o = ord(c)
    return (0x0E00 <= o <= 0x109F or 0x1780 <= o <= 0x17FF or 0x1950 <= o <= 0x19DF or 0x1A20 <= o <= 0x1AAF
            or 0x1B00 <= o <= 0x1B7F or 0xA980 <= o <= 0xA9FF or 0xAA60 <= o <= 0xAADF or 0x3005 <= o <= 0x3007 or 0x3040 <= o <= 0x30FF or 0x31F0 <= o <= 0x31FF
            or 0x3400 <= o <= 0x4DBF or 0x4E00 <= o <= 0x9FFF or 0xF900 <= o <= 0xFAFF or 0xFF66 <= o <= 0xFF9F
            or 0x20000 <= o <= 0x323AF)


OUT = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "..", "crates", "scrutate", "data", "han_fold.txt")


def main() -> int:
    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
        print(__doc__.strip().splitlines()[-1], file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    text = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8").read()
    version = re.search(r"^# Unicode Version (\S+)", text, re.M)
    if not version:
        print("no '# Unicode Version' line in the file header", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    fold: dict[str, str] = {}
    for line in text.splitlines():
        f = line.split("\t")
        if len(f) != 3 or f[1] != "kSimplifiedVariant":
            continue
        src = chr(int(f[0][2:], 16))
        targets = [chr(int(v.split("<")[0][2:], 16)) for v in f[2].split()]
        to = next((t for t in targets if t != src), None)
        if to is not None:
            fold[src] = to
    chained = 0
    for src in fold:
        seen, to = {src}, fold[src]
        while to in fold and fold[to] not in seen:
            seen.add(to)
            to = fold[to]
            chained += 1
        fold[src] = to
    fold = {s: t for s, t in fold.items() if s != t and unspaced(s) and unspaced(t)}
    pairs = "".join(s + fold[s] for s in sorted(fold))
    with open(OUT, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as f:
        f.write(f"# Unihan {version.group(1)} kSimplifiedVariant, traditional then simplified, by tools/gen_han_fold.py\n")
        f.write(pairs + "\n")
    non_bmp = sum(1 for s, t in fold.items() if ord(s) > 0xFFFF or ord(t) > 0xFFFF)
    print(f"wrote {os.path.relpath(OUT)}: {len(fold)} pairs (Unicode {version.group(1)}), {non_bmp} outside the BMP, "
          f"{chained} chain steps followed", file=sys.stderr)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3 """Run every quality gate and record the actual output in docs/TEST_RESULTS.md. Gates: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy -D warnings (both crates), cargo test (core), cargo audit, Python tests of the training code and the benchmark builders, bindings tests (if the wheel is installed), ranking quality against its floor, differential test against ripgrep, reproducible-build check (optional, slow), core test without Python on PATH. DOC_HEAD = """
