#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Verify one Linux platform from a clean container: build and cargo test on an image with no Python
# at all, the static musl binary (statically linked, byte-identical output, timed against glibc),
# and the abi3, cp314t and abi3t wheels installed and tested on several interpreters.
#
#   docker run --rm --platform linux/arm64 -v "$PWD":/src:ro -v "$PWD/bench/results/platforms":/out \
#     rust:1-slim-bookworm bash /src/tools/linux_verify.sh
#
# Results go to /out/linux-<arch>/ (log, wheels, wheel-matrix JSON, musl checks and timing).
set -euo pipefail
arch=$(uname -m)
out=/out/linux-$arch
mkdir -p "$out"
exec > >(tee "$out/verify.log") 2>&1
step() { echo; echo "=== $* ($(date -u +%H:%M:%S))"; }

step "environment"
uname -a
rustc --version
cargo --version
nproc

step "copy source (the mount is read-only; host build output excluded)"
rm -rf /work && mkdir /work
tar -C /src --exclude=./.claude --exclude=./target --exclude=./dist --exclude='.scrutate' --exclude='__pycache__' -cf - . | tar -C /work -xf -
cd /work

step "cargo build + test on an image without Python"
if command -v python3 || command -v python; then echo "unexpected: the base image has Python"; exit 1; fi
cargo build --release -p scrutate --locked
cargo test --release -p scrutate --locked 2>&1 | grep -E '^test result|FAILED|panicked'

step "system packages"
apt-get update -qq
apt-get install -y -qq musl-tools file python3 ripgrep curl git > /dev/null
case "$arch" in
  x86_64) uvsum=c5221ff41b7892bfc223543883600125f6a47fe845093e0f5bdff4f359196d83 ;;
  aarch64) uvsum=71279f8d3c67241e807b9d8db872d1bf541579fb9f08b7d1eb1682196d1e57dc ;;
esac
curl -fsSL -o /tmp/uv.tgz "https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/releases/download/0.13.7/uv-$arch-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz"
echo "$uvsum  /tmp/uv.tgz" | sha256sum -c -
tar -C /usr/local/bin --strip-components=1 -xzf /tmp/uv.tgz
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

step "musl static binary"
musl="$arch-unknown-linux-musl"
rustup target add "$musl"
cargo build --release -p scrutate --locked --target "$musl"
m="target/$musl/release/scrutate"
file "$m" | tee "$out/musl-file.txt"
file "$m" | grep -qE "statically linked|static-pie linked"
if ldd "$m" 2>&1 | grep -q "=>"; then echo "musl binary has dynamic dependencies"; exit 1; fi
untimed() { sed -E 's/"elapsed_ms":[0-9.eE+-]+,?//'; } # the summary's run time differs on every run
for q in '-F fn ' '\w+::\w+\(' '--ident parseFile'; do
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  { target/release/scrutate grep --sort --json $q crates || [ $? -eq 1 ]; } | untimed > /tmp/glibc.jsonl
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  { "$m" grep --sort --json $q crates || [ $? -eq 1 ]; } | untimed > /tmp/musl.jsonl
  cmp /tmp/glibc.jsonl /tmp/musl.jsonl
  echo "identical output for [$q]: $(wc -l < /tmp/glibc.jsonl) lines, $(wc -c < /tmp/glibc.jsonl) bytes"
done | tee "$out/musl-identical.txt"
python3 bench/musl_vs_glibc.py target/release/scrutate "$m" crates --runs 41 | tee "$out/musl-timing.txt"

step "wheels (abi3, cp314t, abi3t)"
uv python install 3.10 3.12 3.13 3.14t 3.15 3.15t
uv tool install maturin
rm -rf target/wheels
maturin build --release --strip -m crates/scrutate-py/Cargo.toml -o target/wheels -i "$(uv python find 3.12)"
maturin build --release --strip -m crates/scrutate-py/Cargo.toml -o target/wheels -i "$(uv python find 3.14t)"
maturin build --release --strip -m crates/scrutate-py/Cargo.toml -o target/wheels -i "$(uv python find 3.15)"
ls target/wheels
uv run --no-project --python 3.12 python tools/wheel_matrix.py --wheels target/wheels --cli "$PWD/target/release/scrutate" \
  --json "$out/wheels.json" 3.10 3.12 3.13 3.14t 3.15 3.15t | tee "$out/wheels.md"

step "done"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Linux x86_64 from an arm64 machine whose x86 emulation cannot run the C compiler (gcc crashes
# with SIGSEGV under Rosetta on the large generated grammar sources): build the binary and every
# test binary for x86_64 natively with a cross toolchain, then run them in an x86_64 container
# with the same paths.
#
#   tools/linux_x86_cross_verify.sh WORK_DIR
#
# The log goes to bench/results/platforms/linux-x86_64/cross-verify.log.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
work=${1:?work directory}
out=bench/results/platforms/linux-x86_64
mkdir -p "$work" "$out"
build='
  set -eo pipefail
  apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y -qq gcc-x86-64-linux-gnu g++-x86-64-linux-gnu libc6-dev-amd64-cross file > /dev/null
  rm -rf /work/src && mkdir -p /work/src
  tar -C /src --exclude=./.claude --exclude=./target --exclude=./dist --exclude=.scrutate --exclude=./fuzz -cf - . | tar -C /work/src -xf -
  cd /work/src
  rustup target add x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu > /dev/null 2>&1
  export CC_x86_64_unknown_linux_gnu=x86_64-linux-gnu-gcc CXX_x86_64_unknown_linux_gnu=x86_64-linux-gnu-g++ \
    CARGO_TARGET_X86_64_UNKNOWN_LINUX_GNU_LINKER=x86_64-linux-gnu-gcc
  cargo build --release -p scrutate --locked --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -q
  cargo test --release -p scrutate --locked --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu --no-run 2>&1 | grep -o "(target/[^)]*)" | tr -d "()" > /work/tests.txt
  file target/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/release/scrutate
  echo "test binaries: $(wc -l < /work/tests.txt)"'
run='
  set -eo pipefail
  cd /work/src
  uname -m
  target/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/release/scrutate --version
  fail=0
  while read -r t; do
    echo "--- $t"
    "$t" --quiet 2>&1 | grep -E "^test result|FAILED|panicked" || fail=1
  done < /work/tests.txt
  exit $fail'
{
  echo "=== cross build on linux/arm64 ($(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ))"
  docker run --rm --platform linux/arm64 -v "$PWD":/src:ro -v "$work":/work rust:1-slim-bookworm bash -c "$build"
  echo "=== tests on linux/amd64"
  docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 -v "$work":/work rust:1-slim-bookworm bash -c "$run"
  echo "=== done"
} 2>&1 | tee "$out/cross-verify.log"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# macOS x86_64 on an Apple Silicon Mac: build the x86_64 binary and wheels, run the Rust test suite
# and the wheel matrix with x86_64 interpreters, all executed by Rosetta 2. This verifies the
# x86_64 build and its behaviour on macOS; it is not a measurement of Intel hardware. Without
# Rosetta 2 (`softwareupdate --install-rosetta`) only the build and the test compilation run.
#   tools/macos_x86_verify.sh
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
out=bench/results/platforms/macos-x86_64
mkdir -p "$out"
exec > >(tee "$out/verify.log") 2>&1
t=x86_64-apple-darwin
export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target/x86
rustup target add "$t"
echo "=== build"
cargo build --release -p scrutate --locked --target "$t"
file "$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/$t/release/scrutate"
if ! /usr/bin/arch -x86_64 /bin/ls / > /dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "=== Rosetta 2 is not installed: x86_64 code cannot run here; compiling the tests only"
  cargo test --release -p scrutate --locked --target "$t" --no-run
  echo "=== done (build only)"
  exit 0
fi
"$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/$t/release/scrutate" --version
echo "=== cargo test (x86_64, under Rosetta 2)"
cargo test --release -p scrutate --locked --target "$t" 2>&1 | grep -E '^test result|FAILED|panicked'
echo "=== wheels"
uv python install cpython-3.10-macos-x86_64-none cpython-3.12-macos-x86_64-none cpython-3.13-macos-x86_64-none > /dev/null
rm -rf "$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/wheels"
maturin build --release --strip -m crates/scrutate-py/Cargo.toml --target "$t" -o "$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/wheels" \
  -i "$(uv python find cpython-3.12-macos-x86_64-none)"
ls "$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/wheels"
uv run --no-project --python 3.13 python tools/wheel_matrix.py --wheels "$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/wheels" --cli "$PWD/$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/$t/release/scrutate" \
  --json "$out/wheels.json" cpython-3.10-macos-x86_64-none cpython-3.12-macos-x86_64-none cpython-3.13-macos-x86_64-none | tee "$out/wheels.md"
echo "=== done"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Network file system check: a copy of a repository on a mounted network share (SMB, NFS, ...)
# must give the same Engine A output as the local copy, and Engine B must index it, answer from
# it, survive concurrent updates and pass `check --files`.
#   tools/netfs_check.sh MOUNTED_DIR LOCAL_REPO
set -euo pipefail
# `scrutate grep` with no path searches a piped standard input
exec < /dev/null
S=${SCRUTATE_BIN:-$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)/target/release/scrutate}
mnt=$1; src=$2
work="$mnt/netfs-check"
rm -rf "$work" && mkdir -p "$work"
(cd "$src" && tar --exclude=.scrutate --exclude=.git -cf - .) | (cd "$work" && tar -xf -)
cd "$work"
echo "file system: $(mount | grep -F " on $(cd "$mnt" && pwd) " | sed 's/.* (//; s/,.*//')"
for q in "-F Searcher" "-i -F error" "[A-Z][a-z]+Builder"; do
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  a=$("$S" grep --sort $q | shasum | cut -c1-16); b=$(cd "$src" && "$S" grep --sort $q | shasum | cut -c1-16)
  echo "engine A [$q]: network $a local $b"
  [ "$a" = "$b" ] || { echo DIFFERENT; exit 1; }
done
"$S" index > /dev/null
echo "engine B index: $("$S" stats | head -c 160)"
for round in 1 2 3; do
  f=$(find . -name '*.rs' | sort | head -1)
  echo "// netfs edit $round" >> "$f"
  pids=""
  for k in 1 2 3; do "$S" index > "/tmp/netfs-$k.log" 2>&1 & pids="$pids $!"; done
  for k in 1 2 3; do "$S" search "builder" -k 2 > /dev/null; "$S" grep --index -F Searcher > /dev/null; done
  for p in $pids; do wait "$p" || { echo "concurrent index failed:"; cat /tmp/netfs-*.log; exit 1; }; done
done
"$S" index > /dev/null
"$S" check --files | tail -1
a=$("$S" grep --index --sort -F 'netfs edit 3' | wc -l | tr -d ' '); b=$("$S" grep --sort -F 'netfs edit 3' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
echo "indexed grep after concurrent updates: $a line(s), walk: $b line(s)"
[ "$a" = "$b" ] || { echo DIFFERENT; exit 1; }
rm -f /tmp/netfs-*.log
cd / && { rm -rf "$work" 2>/dev/null || echo "(cleanup: the share still holds a lock file; removed on the next run)"; }
echo "NETWORK FS OK"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Write or check crates/scrutate/startup.order, the linker order file of the macOS executable.

The file lists the functions a small `scrutate grep` runs, so the linker puts them next to each
other and a search touches fewer pages of the 12 MB of code. ld64 places what it finds and
passes over a name it does not find, so a stale file costs pages, never the build.

usage: order_file.py [--dirs DIR...]  regenerate (macOS on Apple silicon, about 15 minutes: two
                                      release links with a link map, each run under lldb)
       order_file.py --check          the share of the listed names the release links still have

The functions are found by running each release link under lldb with a breakpoint on every
function of its link map, so the names are those of that very link, the standard library's
included. Names carry a hash of how their crate was built, which differs between `cargo build
--release` and `cargo build --release --target aarch64-apple-darwin` (the release workflow): the
file holds the names of both. The release profile links one object (fat LTO, one codegen unit),
so ld64 can place every function; with ThinLTO it passes over the promoted `.llvm.N` functions
and the local ones several objects hold. Needs lldb (Xcode's command line tools). On one machine
processes started under lldb came to hang in dyld's open of their own executable when started
from the build's path, so lldb runs a copy of it; the tool gives up after a minute a search
(`ORDER_FILE_SEARCH_SECONDS` raises that on a busy machine).
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

ROOT = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), ".."))
ORDER = os.path.join(ROOT, "crates", "scrutate", "startup.order")
WORK = os.path.join(ROOT, "target", "order-file")
TARGET = "aarch64-apple-darwin"
# the searches whose functions go first: the start-up row of the benchmarks, then the shapes
# of the other rows, on one file and on a small tree
SEARCHES = [
    ["-F", "-e", "zqxjkvbw_never_present_symbol"],
    ["-F", "-e", "hello"],
    ["-e", "hel+o"],
    ["-F", "-i", "-e", "hello"],
    ["-F", "-w", "-e", "hello"],
    ["-n", "-l", "hello"],
    ["-c", "hello"],
    # last, so that it only adds what records and JSON output run on top of the plain searches
    ["--json", "-F", "-e", "hello"],
]
# lldb with a breakpoint on every function takes about 20 s a search on an idle machine
SEARCH_SECONDS = int(os.environ.get("ORDER_FILE_SEARCH_SECONDS", "60"))
HEADER = (
    "# The functions a small `scrutate grep` runs, for ld64's -order_file (build.rs passes it on\n"
    "# macOS). Written by tools/order_file.py; names a link no longer has are passed over.\n"
)


def run(cmd, **kw):
    print("+", " ".join(cmd), file=sys.stderr)
    return subprocess.run(cmd, check=True, **kw)


def cargo_env(target_dir):
    env = dict(os.environ, CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target_dir)
    env.pop("RUSTFLAGS", None)
    return env


def link_map(target):
    """The executable of a release link and {mangled name: [addresses]} of its __text symbols."""
    tag = target or "host"
    path = os.path.join(WORK, f"{tag}.map")
    cmd = ["cargo", "rustc", "--release", "-p", "scrutate", "--bin", "scrutate", "--locked"] + (["--target", target] if target else [])
    run(cmd + ["--", "-C", f"link-arg=-Wl,-map,{path}"], cwd=ROOT, env=cargo_env(os.path.join(ROOT, "target")))
    exe = os.path.join(ROOT, "target", *([target] if target else []), "release", "scrutate")
    symbols, text, mode = {}, None, None
    for line in open(path, errors="replace"):
        if line.startswith("# Sections"):
            mode = "sec"
        elif line.startswith("# Symbols"):
            mode = "sym"
        elif line.startswith("# Dead Stripped"):
            break
        elif line.startswith("#"):
            continue
        elif mode == "sec":
            p = line.split("\t")
            if len(p) >= 4 and p[3].strip() == "__text":
                text = (int(p[0], 16), int(p[0], 16) + int(p[1], 16))
        elif mode == "sym" and line.startswith("0x"):
            p = line.rstrip("\n").split("\t")
            if text and text[0] <= int(p[0], 16) < text[1]:
                # several objects can hold a local function of one name
                symbols.setdefault(p[2].split("]", 1)[1].strip(), []).append(int(p[0], 16))
    return exe, symbols


def traced(exe, symbols, dirs):
    """The functions of `symbols` that `exe` runs in the searches, first runs first."""
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        job = os.path.join(tmp, "job.json")
        out = os.path.join(tmp, "out.json")
        runs = [(["grep"] + args, where) for args in SEARCHES for where in dirs]
        # under lldb a start from the build's own path came to hang in dyld's open of the executable,
        # where a copy of the same file starts: the copy is what runs
        copy = os.path.join(tmp, "scrutate")
        shutil.copy2(exe, copy)
        with open(job, "w") as f:
            json.dump({"exe": copy, "out": out, "runs": runs, "addrs": symbols}, f)
        # a fresh executable's first start is the one the system scans; under lldb it can hang there
        subprocess.run([copy, "--version"], stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, check=True)
        try:
            run(["lldb", "--batch", "--no-lldbinit", "-o", f"command script import {os.path.abspath(__file__)}"], env=dict(os.environ, ORDER_FILE_JOB=job), timeout=SEARCH_SECONDS * len(runs))
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            sys.exit(f"lldb took over {SEARCH_SECONDS} s a search on {exe}; is the process stuck before main, or the machine busy (ORDER_FILE_SEARCH_SECONDS)?")
        return json.load(open(out))


def __lldb_init_module(debugger, _dict):
    """Inside lldb: run each search with a breakpoint on every function, noting the first hit."""
    import lldb

    job = json.load(open(os.environ["ORDER_FILE_JOB"]))
    names = {addrs[0]: n for n, addrs in job["addrs"].items()}
    debugger.SetAsync(False)
    order, seen = [], set()
    for args, where in job["runs"]:
        target = debugger.CreateTarget(job["exe"])
        info = target.GetLaunchInfo()
        info.SetArguments(args, False)
        info.SetWorkingDirectory(where)
        info.AddOpenFileAction(0, "/dev/null", True, False)
        info.AddOpenFileAction(1, "/dev/null", False, True)
        info.SetLaunchFlags(info.GetLaunchFlags() | lldb.eLaunchFlagDisableASLR | lldb.eLaunchFlagStopAtEntry)
        err = lldb.SBError()
        process = target.Launch(info, err)
        if not err.Success():
            raise SystemExit(f"lldb could not start {job['exe']}: {err}")
        slide = target.GetModuleAtIndex(0).GetObjectFileHeaderAddress().GetLoadAddress(target) - 0x100000000
        at = {}
        for a in names:
            if a not in seen:
                at[target.BreakpointCreateByAddress(a + slide).GetID()] = a
        process.Continue()
        while process.GetState() == lldb.eStateStopped:
            for thread in process:
                if thread.GetStopReason() == lldb.eStopReasonBreakpoint:
                    bid = thread.GetStopReasonDataAtIndex(0)
                    if bid in at:
                        target.FindBreakpointByID(bid).SetEnabled(False)
                        if at[bid] not in seen:
                            seen.add(at[bid])
                            order.append(names[at[bid]])
            process.Continue()
        debugger.DeleteTarget(target)
    json.dump(order, open(job["out"], "w"))


def generate(dirs):
    os.makedirs(WORK, exist_ok=True)

    def searched(dirs):
        lines = [HEADER]
        for target in (None, TARGET):
            exe, symbols = link_map(target)
            names = traced(exe, symbols, dirs)
            # names ld64 would pass over if the profile went back to ThinLTO
            kept = [n for n in names if ".llvm." not in n and len(symbols[n]) == 1]
            print(f"{target or 'host'}: {len(names)} functions ran, {len(kept)} placeable", file=sys.stderr)
            lines += [f"{n}\n" for n in kept]
        with open(ORDER, "w") as f:
            f.writelines(dict.fromkeys(lines))
        print(f"{ORDER} has {len(dict.fromkeys(lines)) - 1} lines")

    if dirs:
        return searched([os.path.abspath(d) for d in dirs])
    # outside any repository, as the benchmark's directories are: a repository's ignore files
    # would bring in their own code
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tree:
        with open(os.path.join(tree, "a.txt"), "w") as f:
            f.write("hello\n")
        os.makedirs(os.path.join(tree, "src", "sub"))
        for i, d in enumerate(["src", "src/sub"]):
            with open(os.path.join(tree, d, f"{i}.rs"), "w") as f:
                f.write("fn main() { println!(\"hello\"); }\n")
        return searched([tree, os.path.join(tree, "src")])


def check():
    os.makedirs(WORK, exist_ok=True)
    listed = [l.rstrip("\n").split(":")[-1] for l in open(ORDER) if l.strip() and not l.startswith("#")]
    have = set(link_map(None)[1]) | set(link_map(TARGET)[1])
    found = sum(n in have for n in dict.fromkeys(listed))
    total = len(dict.fromkeys(listed))
    print(f"{found} of {total} names of {os.path.relpath(ORDER, ROOT)} are in the release links ({100 * found / total:.0f}%)")
    return 0 if found * 2 >= total else 1


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--check", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--dirs", nargs="+", default=[], help="directories to search instead of a small tree made for the purpose")
    if sys.platform != "darwin":
        sys.exit("the order file is made from ld64 link maps: run this on macOS")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    return check() if a.check else generate(a.dirs) or 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the release artifacts for the current platform without CI: binary tarball, wheels, SBOM and
# checksums. The release workflow does the same for every platform and adds Sigstore attestations.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
# .cargo/config.toml sets it for cargo; maturin reads it from the environment for the wheel tag
export MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=${MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET:-13.0}
v=$(grep -m1 '^version = ' crates/scrutate/Cargo.toml | cut -d'"' -f2)
target=$(rustc -vV | sed -n 's/^host: //p')
rm -rf dist && mkdir -p dist
cargo build --release -p scrutate --locked
# the binary must need only the operating system's own libraries
if command -v otool > /dev/null; then
  if otool -L target/release/scrutate | tail -n +2 | grep -v -E '^[[:space:]]+(/usr/lib/|/System/)'; then
    echo "target/release/scrutate links a library outside the system"; exit 1
  fi
elif command -v ldd > /dev/null; then
  if ldd target/release/scrutate | grep -v -E 'linux-vdso|ld-linux|lib(c|m|dl|pthread|rt|gcc_s)\.so'; then
    echo "target/release/scrutate links a library outside the system"; exit 1
  fi
fi
name="scrutate-$v-$target"
rm -rf "dist/$name" && mkdir -p "dist/$name"
cp target/release/scrutate LICENSE-APACHE LICENSE-MIT README.md CHANGELOG.md "dist/$name/"
python3 tools/third_party_notices.py --out "dist/$name/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt"
# tracked files only: a note or a .DS_Store left in the working tree must not ship
if git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree > /dev/null 2>&1; then
  git archive HEAD docs integrations | tar -x -C "dist/$name"
else
  cp -r docs integrations "dist/$name/"
fi
tar -C dist -czf "dist/$name.tar.gz" "$name"
rm -rf "dist/$name"
# the installers (the GitHub action, the GitLab and Bitbucket templates) check the archive against this
(cd dist && sha256sum "$name.tar.gz" > "$name.sha256")
if command -v maturin >/dev/null; then
  for f in LICENSE-APACHE LICENSE-MIT; do
    cmp -s "$f" "crates/scrutate-py/$f" || { echo "crates/scrutate-py/$f (the wheel's copy) differs from $f"; exit 1; }
  done
  python3 tools/third_party_notices.py --package scrutate-py --out crates/scrutate-py/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt
  # one wheel per kind: cp39-abi3 (standard CPython up to 3.14), cp314t, abi3t (3.15 and newer)
  if command -v uv > /dev/null; then
    pys=""
    for pv in 3.12 3.14t 3.15; do
      pys="$pys $(uv python find "$pv")" || { echo "no Python $pv for its wheel: uv python install $pv"; exit 1; }
    done
  else pys=python3; fi
  for py in $pys; do maturin build --release --strip -m crates/scrutate-py/Cargo.toml -o dist -i "$py"; done
fi
python3 tools/sbom.py --out "dist/scrutate-$v.cdx.json"
(cd dist && sha256sum -- *.tar.gz *.whl *.cdx.json > SHA256SUMS)
echo "artifacts:"; ls -la dist

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproducible build across two different build environments: slim Debian (the Rust image) and full
# Debian (a non-Rust image with rustup installed at the same paths), each a fresh container with the
# same source path. Both build with the toolchain pinned in rust-toolchain.toml. The release
# binaries must have the same SHA-256.
#   tools/repro_docker.sh
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
out=bench/results/platforms/repro
mkdir -p "$out"
rm -f "$out"/*.txt
build='
  set -eo pipefail
  export CARGO_HOME=/usr/local/cargo RUSTUP_HOME=/usr/local/rustup PATH=/usr/local/cargo/bin:$PATH
  if ! command -v rustup > /dev/null; then
    curl -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y -q --profile minimal --default-toolchain none > /dev/null
  fi
  mkdir -p /build && tar -C /src --exclude=./.claude --exclude=./target --exclude=./dist --exclude=.scrutate --exclude=./fuzz -cf - . | tar -C /build -xf -
  cd /build && cargo build --release -p scrutate --locked -q
  sha256sum target/release/scrutate | cut -d" " -f1
  rustc --version
  . /etc/os-release && echo "$PRETTY_NAME"'
for img in rust:1-slim-bookworm golang:1.26-bookworm; do
  tag=${img//[:.]/_}
  docker run --rm --platform linux/arm64 -v "$PWD":/src:ro "$img" bash -c "$build" > "$out/$tag.txt"
  echo "$img: $(tr '\n' ' ' < "$out/$tag.txt")"
done
a=$(head -1 "$out/rust_1-slim-bookworm.txt"); b=$(head -1 "$out/golang_1_26-bookworm.txt")
if [ "$a" = "$b" ]; then echo "REPRODUCIBLE across images: $a"; else echo "NOT REPRODUCIBLE: $a vs $b"; exit 1; fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the release binary twice from clean and compare the hashes. Same toolchain + same source
# path + same flags must give the same bytes; a difference means a reproducibility regression.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
cargo clean -p scrutate --release
cargo build --release -p scrutate --locked -q
h1=$(sha256sum target/release/scrutate | cut -d' ' -f1)
cargo clean -p scrutate --release
cargo build --release -p scrutate --locked -q
h2=$(sha256sum target/release/scrutate | cut -d' ' -f1)
echo "build 1: $h1"
echo "build 2: $h2"
if [ "$h1" = "$h2" ]; then echo "REPRODUCIBLE"; else echo "NOT REPRODUCIBLE"; exit 1; fi

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Software bill of materials (CycloneDX 1.5 JSON) from the resolved Cargo dependency graph.

Uses `cargo metadata` (the authoritative, locked graph) so the SBOM lists exactly what the binary
was built from: name, version, license expression, source registry and purl for every crate, and
one `data` component per data file from outside the project (`third_party_notices.data_files`).

usage: sbom.py [--out FILE] [--package scrutate]
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import uuid

from third_party_notices import data_files

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--out", default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--package", default="scrutate")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    meta = json.loads(subprocess.run(["cargo", "metadata", "--format-version", "1", "--locked"], cwd=os.path.join(HERE, ".."), capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout)
    by_id = {p["id"]: p for p in meta["packages"]}
    nodes = {n["id"]: n for n in meta["resolve"]["nodes"]}
    root_id = next(p["id"] for p in meta["packages"] if p["name"] == a.package)
    # transitive closure of normal + build dependencies (dev dependencies are not shipped)
    seen, stack = set(), [root_id]
    while stack:
        nid = stack.pop()
        if nid in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(nid)
        for dep in nodes[nid]["deps"]:
            if any(k["kind"] in (None, "build") for k in dep["dep_kinds"]):
                stack.append(dep["pkg"])
    comps = []
    for nid in sorted(seen - {root_id}, key=lambda i: (by_id[i]["name"], by_id[i]["version"])):
        p = by_id[nid]
        comps.append({
            "type": "library",
            "bom-ref": f"pkg:cargo/{p['name']}@{p['version']}",
            "name": p["name"],
            "version": p["version"],
            "purl": f"pkg:cargo/{p['name']}@{p['version']}",
            "licenses": [{"expression": p["license"]}] if p.get("license") else [],
            "externalReferences": [{"type": "distribution", "url": p["source"] or "path"}] + ([{"type": "website", "url": p["repository"]}] if p.get("repository") else []),
        })
        if not p["source"]:
            # a crate vendored under vendor/ with local changes (see the workspace Cargo.toml)
            rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.dirname(p["manifest_path"]), os.path.join(HERE, ".."))
            comps[-1]["pedigree"] = {"notes": f"modified copy of the crates.io release, in {rel}"}
            comps[-1]["externalReferences"][0]["url"] = rel
    for d in data_files():
        comps.append({
            "type": "data",
            "bom-ref": f"data:{d['name']}@{d['version']}",
            "name": d["name"],
            "version": d["version"],
            "description": d["purpose"],
            "licenses": [{"expression": d["license"]}],
            "externalReferences": [{"type": "distribution", "url": d["url"]}],
            "pedigree": {"notes": f"derived file, compiled in from {d['file']}"},
        })
    root = by_id[root_id]
    bom = {
        "bomFormat": "CycloneDX",
        "specVersion": "1.5",
        "serialNumber": f"urn:uuid:{uuid.uuid4()}",
        "version": 1,
        "metadata": {
            "timestamp": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()),
            "tools": [{"name": "scrutate/tools/sbom.py", "version": root["version"]}],
            "component": {"type": "application", "bom-ref": f"pkg:cargo/{root['name']}@{root['version']}", "name": root["name"], "version": root["version"],
                          "licenses": [{"expression": root["license"]}] if root.get("license") else []},
        },
        "components": comps,
        "dependencies": [
            {"ref": f"pkg:cargo/{by_id[nid]['name']}@{by_id[nid]['version']}",
             "dependsOn": sorted({f"pkg:cargo/{by_id[d['pkg']]['name']}@{by_id[d['pkg']]['version']}" for d in nodes[nid]["deps"] if d["pkg"] in seen})}
            for nid in sorted(seen, key=lambda i: by_id[i]["name"])
        ],
    }
    text = json.dumps(bom, indent=1)
    if a.out:
        with open(a.out, "w") as f:
            f.write(text)
        print(f"{len(comps)} components -> {a.out}", file=sys.stderr)
    else:
        print(text)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Write `~` for this machine's home directory in the committed results and generated documents.

usage: scrub_home.py [--check]

Logs and result files record absolute paths of the machine that made them. This rewrites the
tracked text files under bench/results and docs in place; with --check it changes nothing and
exits 1 when a file still names the home directory.
"""
import os
import subprocess
import sys

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))


def main() -> int:
    check = "--check" in sys.argv[1:]
    home = os.path.expanduser("~").rstrip("/").encode()
    assert home.count(b"/") >= 2, home  # never "/" or a one-part path
    files = subprocess.run(["git", "ls-files", "-z", "bench/results", "docs"], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, check=True).stdout.split(b"\0")
    hit = 0
    for rel in filter(None, files):
        if rel.startswith(b"docs/research/"):
            continue  # notes that are left as they were written
        path = os.path.join(ROOT.encode(), rel)
        try:
            with open(path, "rb") as f:
                data = f.read()
        except OSError:
            continue
        if b"\0" in data[:8192] or home not in data:
            continue
        hit += 1
        if check:
            print(rel.decode())
        else:
            with open(path, "wb") as f:
                f.write(data.replace(home, b"~"))
    print(f"{hit} file(s) {'name' if check else 'named'} the home directory")
    return 1 if check and hit else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""The licence and notice files of every crate compiled into the binary, in one text file.

MIT, BSD and Apache-2.0 all ask that their notices travel with the binary; release archives
include this file next to LICENSE-APACHE and LICENSE-MIT. The crate set is the one
`tools/sbom.py` lists (normal and build dependencies of the package, from the locked
`cargo metadata` graph). A crate that ships no licence file is listed with its declared licence
expression, so the gap is visible. Data files
from outside the project (`data_files`, the Unihan-derived Han fold) come first, with their licence.

usage: third_party_notices.py [--out FILE] [--package scrutate]
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
NAMES = ("license", "licence", "copying", "notice", "unlicense", "copyright")
MIT = """Permission is hereby granted, free of charge, to any person obtaining a copy of this software
and associated documentation files (the "Software"), to deal in the Software without restriction,
including without limitation the rights to use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute,
sublicense, and/or sell copies of the Software, and to permit persons to whom the Software is
furnished to do so, subject to the following conditions:

The above copyright notice and this permission notice shall be included in all copies or
substantial portions of the Software.

THE SOFTWARE IS PROVIDED "AS IS", WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING BUT
NOT LIMITED TO THE WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE AND
NONINFRINGEMENT. IN NO EVENT SHALL THE AUTHORS OR COPYRIGHT HOLDERS BE LIABLE FOR ANY CLAIM, DAMAGES
OR OTHER LIABILITY, WHETHER IN AN ACTION OF CONTRACT, TORT OR OTHERWISE, ARISING FROM, OUT OF OR IN
CONNECTION WITH THE SOFTWARE OR THE USE OR OTHER DEALINGS IN THE SOFTWARE."""


def shipped(package: str) -> list[dict]:
    meta = json.loads(subprocess.run(["cargo", "metadata", "--format-version", "1", "--locked"], cwd=os.path.join(HERE, ".."),
                                     capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout)
    by_id = {p["id"]: p for p in meta["packages"]}
    nodes = {n["id"]: n for n in meta["resolve"]["nodes"]}
    root = next(p["id"] for p in meta["packages"] if p["name"] == package)
    seen, stack = set(), [root]
    while stack:
        nid = stack.pop()
        if nid in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(nid)
        for dep in nodes[nid]["deps"]:
            if any(k["kind"] in (None, "build") for k in dep["dep_kinds"]):
                stack.append(dep["pkg"])
    return sorted((by_id[i] for i in seen - {root}), key=lambda p: (p["name"], p["version"]))


# C libraries compiled into the binary whose licence lives only in their source headers
BUNDLED = {"pcre2-sys": ("PCRE2", "upstream/src/pcre2_compile.c")}

UNICODE_V3 = """UNICODE LICENSE V3

COPYRIGHT AND PERMISSION NOTICE

Copyright © 1991-2026 Unicode, Inc.

NOTICE TO USER: Carefully read the following legal agreement. BY
DOWNLOADING, INSTALLING, COPYING OR OTHERWISE USING DATA FILES, AND/OR
SOFTWARE, YOU UNEQUIVOCALLY ACCEPT, AND AGREE TO BE BOUND BY, ALL OF THE
TERMS AND CONDITIONS OF THIS AGREEMENT. IF YOU DO NOT AGREE, DO NOT
DOWNLOAD, INSTALL, COPY, DISTRIBUTE OR USE THE DATA FILES OR SOFTWARE.

Permission is hereby granted, free of charge, to any person obtaining a
copy of data files and any associated documentation (the "Data Files") or
software and any associated documentation (the "Software") to deal in the
Data Files or Software without restriction, including without limitation
the rights to use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute, and/or sell
copies of the Data Files or Software, and to permit persons to whom the
Data Files or Software are furnished to do so, provided that either (a)
this copyright and permission notice appear with all copies of the Data
Files or Software, or (b) this copyright and permission notice appear in
associated Documentation.

THE DATA FILES AND SOFTWARE ARE PROVIDED "AS IS", WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY
KIND, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO THE WARRANTIES OF
MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE AND NONINFRINGEMENT OF
THIRD PARTY RIGHTS.

IN NO EVENT SHALL THE COPYRIGHT HOLDER OR HOLDERS INCLUDED IN THIS NOTICE
BE LIABLE FOR ANY CLAIM, OR ANY SPECIAL INDIRECT OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES,
OR ANY DAMAGES WHATSOEVER RESULTING FROM LOSS OF USE, DATA OR PROFITS,
WHETHER IN AN ACTION OF CONTRACT, NEGLIGENCE OR OTHER TORTIOUS ACTION,
ARISING OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH THE USE OR PERFORMANCE OF THE DATA
FILES OR SOFTWARE.

Except as contained in this notice, the name of a copyright holder shall
not be used in advertising or otherwise to promote the sale, use or other
dealings in these Data Files or Software without prior written
authorization of the copyright holder."""


def data_files() -> list[dict]:
    """Data from outside the project compiled into the scrutate crate (and so into every package built on it)."""
    path = os.path.join(HERE, "..", "crates", "scrutate", "data", "han_fold.txt")
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        version = f.readline().split()[2]
    return [{"name": "unihan-kSimplifiedVariant", "version": version, "license": "Unicode-3.0", "licence_text": UNICODE_V3,
             "url": "https://www.unicode.org/Public/UCD/latest/ucd/Unihan.zip", "file": "crates/scrutate/data/han_fold.txt",
             "purpose": "traditional-to-simplified Han fold of ranked search, from the Unihan field kSimplifiedVariant (tools/gen_han_fold.py)"}]


def header_licence(path: str) -> str:
    """The comment of a C source file that holds its licence (copyright lines included)."""
    text = open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
    at = text.find("Redistribution and use")
    if at < 0:
        return ""
    start = text.rfind("/*", 0, at)
    end = text.find("*/", at)
    return text[start:end + 2]


def licence_files(manifest_path: str) -> list[str]:
    d = os.path.dirname(manifest_path)
    found = []
    for f in sorted(os.listdir(d)):
        full = os.path.join(d, f)
        if os.path.isfile(full) and f.lower().split(".")[0].split("-")[0].split("_")[0] in NAMES:
            found.append(full)
    return found


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--out", default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--package", default="scrutate")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    pkgs = shipped(a.package)
    data = data_files()
    out = [f"Third-party software in {a.package}: {len(pkgs)} crates and {len(data)} data file(s), with their licence and notice files.",
           "Scrutate's own code is under MIT OR Apache-2.0, at your option (LICENSE-MIT, LICENSE-APACHE); this file",
           "covers only what it compiles in from others.", ""]
    for d in data:
        out.append("=" * 78)
        out.append(f"{d['name']} {d['version']}  ({d['license']}), data compiled in as {d['file']}")
        out.append(d["url"])
        out.append(d["purpose"])
        out.append("-" * 78)
        out.append(d["licence_text"])
        out.append("")
    missing = 0
    for p in pkgs:
        out.append("=" * 78)
        out.append(f"{p['name']} {p['version']}  ({p.get('license') or 'no licence expression'})")
        if p.get("repository"):
            out.append(p["repository"])
        files = licence_files(p["manifest_path"])
        if not files:
            missing += 1
            holders = ", ".join(p.get("authors") or []) or f"the {p['name']} authors (see the repository)"
            out.append(f"The crate ships no licence file. Copyright (c) {holders}. Licensed under {p.get('license') or 'the terms in its repository'};")
            out.append("the standard texts of those licences are at the end of this file.")
        for f in files:
            out.append("-" * 78)
            out.append(os.path.basename(f))
            out.append("")
            out.append(open(f, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read().rstrip())
        if p["name"] in BUNDLED:
            lib, rel = BUNDLED[p["name"]]
            src = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(p["manifest_path"]), rel)
            out.append("-" * 78)
            out.append(f"{lib}, the C library this crate compiles in (licence from {rel})")
            out.append("")
            out.append(header_licence(src) if os.path.exists(src) else f"({rel} not found; see the {lib} project)")
        out.append("")
    out.append("=" * 78)
    out.append("Standard licence texts, for the crates above that ship no licence file")
    out.append("-" * 78)
    out.append("MIT License")
    out.append("")
    out.append(MIT)
    out.append("-" * 78)
    out.append("Apache License 2.0 (the full text, as in this project's LICENSE-APACHE)")
    out.append("")
    out.append(open(os.path.join(HERE, "..", "LICENSE-APACHE"), encoding="utf-8").read().rstrip())
    text = "\n".join(out) + "\n"
    if a.out:
        with open(a.out, "w") as f:
            f.write(text)
        print(f"wrote {a.out}: {len(pkgs)} crates, {missing} without a licence file, {len(data)} data file(s)", file=sys.stderr)
    else:
        sys.stdout.write(text)
    return 0

    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Count PASS / PARTIAL / BLOCKED / FAIL rows in docs/TRACEABILITY.md (a row with a mixed status
counts as its weakest) and rewrite the tally lines, so the summary can never drift from the table."""
import os
import re

p = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "..", "docs", "TRACEABILITY.md")
s = open(p).read()
counts = {"PASS": 0, "PARTIAL": 0, "BLOCKED": 0, "FAIL": 0}
for line in s.splitlines():
    if not line.startswith("| ") or line.startswith("| ID") or line.startswith("| Gate") or line.startswith("|---"):
        continue
    cells = [c.strip() for c in line.strip().strip("|").split("|")]
    # section 8 and the release-gate table carry the status in the second cell
    for cell in (cells[-1], cells[1] if len(cells) > 1 else ""):
        found = [k for k in ("FAIL", "BLOCKED", "PARTIAL", "PASS") if re.search(rf"\b{k}\b", cell)]
        if found:
            counts[found[0]] += 1
            break
total = sum(counts.values())
line = f"PASS {counts['PASS']} · PARTIAL {counts['PARTIAL']} · BLOCKED {counts['BLOCKED']} · FAIL {counts['FAIL']}"
s = re.sub(r"Counts: PASS \d+ · PARTIAL \d+ · BLOCKED \d+ · FAIL \d+ (\(tallied at the end\)|over \d+ rows \(computed by `tools/traceability_tally.py`\))\.",
           f"Counts: {line} over {total} rows (computed by `tools/traceability_tally.py`).", s)
s = re.sub(r"## Tally\n\nPASS \d+ · PARTIAL \d+ · BLOCKED \d+ · FAIL \d+( over \d+ rows)?\.", f"## Tally\n\n{line} over {total} rows.", s)
open(p, "w").write(s)
print(line, "over", total, "rows")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Install the built wheels into fresh virtual environments, one per interpreter, and run the
bindings tests there.

usage: wheel_matrix.py --wheels DIR --cli PATH [--json OUT] PYTHON...

PYTHON is anything `uv venv --python` accepts (3.12, 3.14t, a path). The installer picks the wheel
from DIR, as it would from an index: cp39-abi3 on a standard interpreter up to 3.14, cp314t on
free-threaded 3.14, and the abi3t wheel on 3.15 and newer, both builds. A free-threaded
interpreter must refuse the abi3 wheel, and its GIL must still be disabled after
`import scrutate`, with warnings treated as errors. Exit status 0 only when every check passed.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import glob
import json
import os
import platform
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

ROOT = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), ".."))


def sh(cmd, **kw):
    r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, **kw)
    return r.returncode, (r.stdout + r.stderr).strip()


def tags(wheel):
    """The tag triples a wheel file name stands for (cp315-abi3.abi3t-x is two)."""
    py, abi, plat = os.path.basename(wheel)[:-4].split("-")[-3:]
    return {f"{p}-{a}-{q}" for p in py.split(".") for a in abi.split(".") for q in plat.split(".")}


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--wheels", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--cli", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--json")
    ap.add_argument("pythons", nargs="+")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    abi3 = glob.glob(os.path.join(a.wheels, "scrutate-*-abi3-*.whl"))
    wheels = glob.glob(os.path.join(a.wheels, "scrutate-*.whl"))
    rows, ok_all = [], True
    for py in a.pythons:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
            venv = os.path.join(d, "v")
            rc, out = sh(["uv", "venv", "-q", "--python", py, venv])
            if rc:
                rows.append({"python": py, "ok": False, "error": out[-400:]})
                ok_all = False
                continue
            exe = os.path.join(venv, "Scripts" if os.name == "nt" else "bin", "python")
            _, info = sh([exe, "-c", "import sys,sysconfig,json,platform;print(json.dumps([sys.version.split()[0], bool(sysconfig.get_config_var('Py_GIL_DISABLED')), platform.system() + ' ' + platform.machine()]))"])
            version, free, arch = json.loads(info.splitlines()[-1])
            row = {"python": version, "free_threaded": free, "platform": arch, "checks": {}}
            if free and abi3:
                rc, out = sh(["uv", "pip", "install", "-q", "--python", exe, abi3[0]])
                row["checks"]["abi3 wheel refused"] = rc != 0
            rc, out = sh(["uv", "pip", "install", "-q", "--python", exe, "--no-index", "--find-links", a.wheels, "scrutate"])
            row["checks"]["installed"] = rc == 0
            if rc == 0:
                _, meta = sh([exe, "-c", "import importlib.metadata as m; print(m.distribution('scrutate').read_text('WHEEL'))"])
                got = {line.split(": ", 1)[1] for line in meta.splitlines() if line.startswith("Tag: ")}
                row["wheel"] = next((os.path.basename(w) for w in wheels if tags(w) == got), "?")
                if free:
                    row["checks"]["free-threaded wheel chosen"] = "t-" in row["wheel"]
                rc, out = sh(["uv", "pip", "install", "-q", "--python", exe, "pytest"])
            if rc == 0:
                probe = "import sys, scrutate; print(getattr(sys, '_is_gil_enabled', lambda: True)())"
                rc, out = sh([exe, "-W", "error", "-c", probe])
                if free:
                    row["checks"]["GIL stays disabled after import (-W error)"] = rc == 0 and out.splitlines()[-1] == "False"
                else:
                    row["checks"]["imports"] = rc == 0
                rc, out = sh([exe, "-m", "pytest", "-q", "-p", "no:cacheprovider", "tests/test_bindings.py"],
                             cwd=os.path.join(ROOT, "python"), env={**os.environ, "SCRUTATE_BIN": os.path.abspath(a.cli)})
                row["checks"]["bindings tests"] = rc == 0
                row["pytest"] = out.splitlines()[-1] if out else ""
            row["ok"] = bool(row["checks"]) and all(row["checks"].values())
            ok_all &= row["ok"]
            rows.append(row)
    host = f"{platform.system()} {platform.machine()}"
    print(f"| Platform | Python | Wheel | Checks | Result |\n|---|---|---|---|---|")
    for r in rows:
        host = r.get("platform", host)
        checks = ", ".join(f"{k}: {'yes' if v else 'NO'}" for k, v in r.get("checks", {}).items()) or r.get("error", "")
        tag = f"{r['python']}{' (free-threaded)' if r.get('free_threaded') else ''}"
        print(f"| {host} | {tag} | {r.get('wheel', '-')} | {checks}; pytest: {r.get('pytest', '-')} | {'PASS' if r['ok'] else 'FAIL'} |")
    if a.json:
        with open(a.json, "w") as f:
            json.dump({"host": host, "platform": platform.platform(), "rows": rows}, f, indent=1)
    return 0 if ok_all else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

ignore
======
The ignore crate provides a fast recursive directory iterator that respects
various filters such as globs, file types and `.gitignore` files. This crate
also provides lower level direct access to gitignore and file type matchers.

[![Build status](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/workflows/ci/badge.svg)](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/actions)
[![](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/ignore.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/ignore)

Dual-licensed under MIT or the [UNLICENSE](https://unlicense.org/).

### Documentation

[https://docs.rs/ignore](https://docs.rs/ignore)

### Usage

Add this to your `Cargo.toml`:

```toml
[dependencies]
ignore = "0.4"
```

### Example

This example shows the most basic usage of this crate. This code will
recursively traverse the current directory while automatically filtering out
files and directories according to ignore globs found in files like
`.ignore` and `.gitignore`:


```rust,no_run
use ignore::Walk;

for result in Walk::new("./") {
    // Each item yielded by the iterator is either a directory entry or an
    // error, so either print the path or the error.
    match result {
        Ok(entry) => println!("{}", entry.path().display()),
        Err(err) => println!("ERROR: {}", err),
    }
}
```

### Example: advanced

By default, the recursive directory iterator will ignore hidden files and
directories. This can be disabled by building the iterator with `WalkBuilder`:

```rust,no_run
use ignore::WalkBuilder;

for result in WalkBuilder::new("./").hidden(false).build() {
    println!("{:?}", result);
}
```

See the documentation for `WalkBuilder` for many other options.

# Workspace discovery benchmarks

`workloads.rs` measures the `ignore` operations used by Python development tools:

| Consumer | Operation | Benchmarks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Ruff file discovery](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/blob/ae8ec3753192debd310e7b3d93255a19a5a2af85/crates/ruff_workspace/src/resolver.rs#L530) and [ty project indexing](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/blob/ae8ec3753192debd310e7b3d93255a19a5a2af85/crates/ruff_db/src/system/os.rs#L312) | Parallel walks, hidden files included, up to 12 workers | `walk_*_parallel_*`, `walk_explicit_files` |
| [uv script discovery](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/83d556d712c7e316932b239c49e86a5de95d124a/crates/uv/src/commands/workspace/list.rs#L137) | Serial traversal with ignore rules and hidden files included | `walk_*_serial`, `uv_scripts_source_archive` |
| [uv workspace discovery](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/83d556d712c7e316932b239c49e86a5de95d124a/crates/uv-workspace/src/workspace.rs#L1931) | Stop at the first non-directory entry, or exhaust an ignored member | `uv_*_workspace_member` |
| [ty incremental indexing](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/blob/ae8ec3753192debd310e7b3d93255a19a5a2af85/crates/ruff_db/src/system/os/ignore.rs#L10) | Repeated relative-path checks with cached ancestor matchers | `incremental_*` |

The synthetic trees contain Python modules, package metadata, non-Python files,
ignored bytecode directories, a virtual environment, and build outputs. The
layouts vary independently: a small project, many sibling packages, deeply
nested packages, and packages with their own ignore rules and negations. The
parallel visitor counts files locally and merges once per worker, avoiding an
artificial shared counter on every entry. One- and four-worker cases supplement
the 12-worker configuration used by Ruff and ty. The unfiltered walk models
disabling ignore rules and provides a control for traversal overhead.
The source-archive case honors `.gitignore` without a `.git` directory, matching
uv's `require_git(false)` configuration.

Fixtures are created before timing and removed afterward. Every walk checks its
Python file count against the fixture's expected count. The benchmarks retain
parent ignore discovery, but disable global Git ignore configuration so that
results do not depend on a user's Git configuration. Runs use a warm filesystem
cache. They measure `ignore`, excluding parsing, configuration resolution, and
other application work; they are not end-to-end application speedups.

`incremental_cold` includes building matchers and loading directory rules on
first use. `incremental_warm` checks 256 paths after their directories have been
cached. `incremental_warm_noncanonical` checks the same paths with an internal
`./` component, exercising normalization during cached queries.
`incremental_ignored` checks a path beneath a pruned virtual environment.
`incremental_warm_deep` checks 768 paths in a 12-level package tree, and
`incremental_ignored_parent` directly hits an ignored directory's cache entry.
`incremental_ignored_nested` checks a deeper descendant of a cached ignored
virtual environment inside an otherwise allowed package.
The `walk_dense_ignore_*` cases put rules in every directory of a deep tree,
providing a control for optimizations that skip directories without rules.
`incremental_dense_ignore_cold` and `incremental_dense_ignore_warm` use the same
tree to check incremental matching when nearly every cached directory has rules.
The `walk_multiple_roots_*` cases pass 64 sibling package directories as roots,
covering parent-matcher reuse when Ruff receives multiple directory arguments.
`walk_with_overrides_and_types` exercises explicitly configured override and
file-type matchers as a control for their more common empty configuration.
The `build_*` and `match_*` microbenchmarks help distinguish compilation and
matching costs from filesystem traversal.
The single-pattern cases cover bytecode exclusions, the directory whitelist
used in Ruff's and uv's root `.ignore` files, and ty's vendored-typeshed whitelist.
`build_single_directory_whitelist` builds that single-rule matcher from an
already populated builder.
The `*gitignore_only*` controls remove `.ignore` and `.git/info/exclude`, covering
projects that rely solely on a `.gitignore` with multiple patterns.
`walk_selected_python_files` uses two positive override patterns, exercising
file-selection rules that match most visited files.

Like the `globset` benchmarks, these use Rust's nightly `test` harness:

```console
cargo +nightly bench -p ignore --bench workloads
cargo +nightly bench -p ignore --bench workloads incremental
```

For comparisons, use the same compiler, profile, fixture parameters, and CPU
affinity for both revisions. Alternate baseline and candidate runs, and retain
the per-run results instead of relying on a single measurement. Parallel walks
also include worker startup and shutdown, which can dominate small projects.

CPU affinity also affects match-index scratch-pool sizing: available parallelism
is cached when the first pool is constructed. Pinning to one CPU therefore
changes pool construction costs as well as scheduling. Report affinity with
results, especially when comparing construction or cached matching costs.

Ruff, uv, and ty enable fat LTO in release builds, while their profiling builds
omit cross-crate LTO. Check promising changes in both configurations, especially
when small matching benchmarks give inconsistent results:

```console
CARGO_PROFILE_BENCH_LTO=fat CARGO_PROFILE_BENCH_CODEGEN_UNITS=16 cargo +nightly bench -p ignore --bench workloads
```

For focused comparisons, pass one benchmark name with `--exact` so that each
case runs in a separate process:

```console
cargo +nightly bench -p ignore --bench workloads -- --exact incremental_ignored_parent
```

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::DEFAULT_TYPES;

    #[test]
    fn default_types_are_sorted() {
        let mut names = DEFAULT_TYPES.iter().map(|(aliases, _)| aliases[0]);
        let Some(mut previous_name) = names.next() else {
            return;
        };
        for name in names {
            assert!(
                name > previous_name,
                r#""{}" should be sorted before "{}" in `DEFAULT_TYPES`"#,
                name,
                previous_name
            );
            previous_name = name;
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn default_types_aliases_are_sorted() {
        for (aliases, _) in DEFAULT_TYPES.iter() {
            assert!(
                aliases.is_sorted(),
                "this alias list is not sorted: {aliases:?}",
            );
        }
    }
}
